release.body:
### Added
- `baguette defaults read` and the Defaults card now list the settings a running app reads but hasn't stored yet (`@AppStorage` defaults, `register(defaults:)`), typed, so you can set them on a fresh install. → [docs](docs/features/defaults/README.md#workflows) ([#116](https://github.com/tddworks/baguette/pull/116))
- `defaults … --relaunch-if-needed` and the Defaults card change an `@AppStorage` setting in the running app at once, relaunching only for keys it read once; the card also filters by key or type and flashes values the app writes. → [docs](docs/features/defaults/README.md#live-or-relaunch) ([#116](https://github.com/tddworks/baguette/pull/116))

### Fixed
- `serve`'s floating panels (Defaults, Status bar, Network, …) no longer slide under the toolbar in a window taller than the device needs. ([#116](https://github.com/tddworks/baguette/pull/116))

## What's Changed
* feat(defaults): list the settings a running app reads but hasn't stored by @hanrw in https://github.com/tddworks/baguette/pull/116


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/tddworks/baguette/compare/v0.2.6...v0.2.7

release.body:
### Added

- iOS: Xcode 27 **Resize Mode** (a "resizable app session", started from Device Hub or `xcrun devicectl device appResize start`) is now detected, and every affected verb is honest about it instead of pretending to work. During a session the frontmost app renders on a virtual `Resizable` display while the main display shows only the wallpaper; every simulator primitive sim-use drives — HID touch, the framebuffer, the accessibility point hit-test — is bound to the main display. `ui` now carries a `resizable_app_session` advisory (`[i] …` in text, top-level `advisory` in `--json`) naming the scene size and the device size; `screenshot` captures the `Resizable` display (the app, at the scene's size) and says so in the same advisory; `tap`, `long-press`, `swipe`, `touch`, `gesture`, `multi-touch`, `paste --via-menu` (a long-press plus menu taps) and a `batch` containing a touch step **fail** with an explanation and a hint instead of reporting a tap that was never delivered; a `batch` re-checks before every touch step, so a session that begins mid-batch, or inside the cache window, stops the batch at its first touch step with nothing sent. `record-video` and `stream-video` fail the same way, before creating a file or emitting a byte — both capture only the main display, and the hint gives the `xcrun simctl io <udid> recordVideo --display=<uuid>` form that records the `Resizable` one. `type`, Cmd+V `paste` and the key verbs are untouched — keyboard HID does reach the resized app. The check is one `xcrun devicectl device info appResize` per device per 5 s (~0.3 s, cached in the daemon) — re-run early when `ui` or a selector tap sees a scene size that is neither the device's own size nor its landscape swap and that it has not probed before, so a session that just started is caught at once while a display whose accessibility size never matches its framebuffer (iPhone mini) pays no more than anyone else; only a scene at exactly the device's own size, and standalone raw `-x/-y` taps, wait out the window. The check runs on every toolchain whose `devicectl` knows the query (Xcode 26.6 does), since another Xcode or Device Hub may own the session; `SIM_USE_RESIZE_SESSION_CHECK=0` disables it (the per-device daemon reads it at spawn). The bundled skill's preflight now requires sim-use 0.15.0 or newer, because its Resize Mode guidance relies on this detection. Real touch routing to the `Resizable` display is a separate, larger piece of work (upstream idb's multi-display plumbing plus the scene geometry) — see `docs/ai/xxxx-resizable-app-session/README.md`. (#143, #150 — thanks @iXerol!)
- Linux build, Android only: `Package.swift` now declares an `#if os(Linux)` target graph (`SimUseCore`, `AndroidBackend`, and a new `SimUseLinux` executable) that builds with a Swift 6 toolchain and drives Android devices exactly as the macOS build does — `ui`, `tap`, `long-press`, `type`, `swipe`, `screenshot`, `app-state`, the `android` namespace and the per-device daemon. `long-press` and `app-state` share their Android implementation with the macOS commands, so flags and JSON match. iOS verbs, video capture, the Viewer and `init` stay macOS-only; on Linux, invoking one prints an error naming the verb instead of a misleading parse error. The macOS manifest is unchanged. `scripts/install-linux.sh` builds and installs it; see `docs/linux.md`. (#141, #147 — thanks @iopass4!)
- Remote adb servers: when `ADB_SERVER_SOCKET` points at another machine (`tcp:<host>:<port>`, e.g. WSL using the Windows host's adb), or `ANDROID_ADB_SERVER_ADDRESS` does when no socket is set, the bridge is reached on that host — where `adb forward` actually listens — instead of `127.0.0.1`. `SIM_USE_BRIDGE_HOST` overrides the host. The cached forward and bridge token are scoped to that connection: switching adb servers restarts the device's daemon and re-creates them, and a session restored from disk is reused only while `adb forward --list` still lists its forward, so a restored token is not sent to another host or to an unrelated listener on the old port. A session that a running daemon already holds is not rechecked before each request, so a forward that another tool changes under it goes unnoticed until a request fails. Each daemon request also carries the client's connection, and a daemon started for another connection refuses the request without running it; this covers a daemon that is too busy with another client's command to answer the restart check in time. This covers every adb serial, including wireless-debugging serials too long for the Android UDID heuristic, and a failed `adb forward --list` is reported instead of opening another forward and leaving the old one registered. Equivalent spellings of the default server (no variables, `ANDROID_ADB_SERVER_PORT=5037`, `tcp:localhost:5037`) count as one connection, so switching between them neither restarts the daemon nor leaves a forward behind; when only the bridge host changes, the old forward is removed before a new one is opened. A forward on a different adb server is left in place (see `docs/linux.md`). `android init` reports the host it reached the bridge on as `http_endpoint` (and `bridgeHost` in `--json`) instead of always printing `localhost`. (#141, #147 — thanks @iopass4!)
- `sim-use android describe-ui` accepts `ui`, matching the top-level verb. (#141, #147 — thanks @iopass4!)
- `tap` accepts `--coordinate-space` for explicit `-x/-y` / `--point` coordinates, matching `swipe` and `touch`. `ui` transforms outline (visual-space) coordinates through the same orientation calibration selector taps already ride, so a coordinate read off `describe-ui` lands where it was read on a rotated device; `native` (device-native portrait, the default) is unchanged and stays zero-cost. Aliases and selectors are already resolved in ui space and reject the flag rather than silently ignoring it. Batch `tap` steps ride the batch-wide calibration, and `android tap` accepts the flag for parity and ignores it. The bundled skill's Act table and pitfalls row now name `tap` alongside `swipe`/`touch`. (#142, #144 — thanks @iXerol!)
- `stream-video --format h264` now works on iOS, not just Android: a native `FBVideoStream` H.264 stream, carried in MPEG-TS, copied straight to stdout with no host-side codec pass. On a booted iPhone 17 Pro this delivers ~24 fps at ~1.3 MB per 6 s, against the screenshot loop's ~4.1 fps at ~11 MB — roughly 5.9x the frame rate for an eighth of the bytes. Preview it with `sim-use stream-video --format h264 --device $UDID | ffplay -f mpegts -probesize 32768 -i -`. It streams at a constant `--fps`, default 30 (the screenshot formats keep their default of 10). MPEG-TS rather than the Android leg's bare Annex B on purpose: Annex B carries no presentation timestamps, so a player paces on a guessed frame rate (ffprobe reads a bare stream as 25 fps regardless of `--fps`) and a 30 fps capture drifts ~5 frames further behind every second, unbounded — minutes of lag within a few minutes of viewing. MPEG-TS carries PTS/DTS, and the player's queue measured empty across a 60 s run. The top-level `stream-video` no longer rejects `h264` for iOS targets, so the only platform-exclusive format left is the experimental iOS-only `bgra`. (#132, #133)

### Changed

- iOS `stream-video --format mjpeg` / `raw` / `ffmpeg` are deprecated and now warn once on stderr, pointing at `--format h264`. On a simulator the screenshot loop has no remaining advantage — `h264` measured 144 frames in 1.33 MB against `mjpeg`'s 24 in 11.2 MB over the same 6 s — and it is available on every booted simulator, so these will be removed in a later release. **Android keeps its equivalents and does not warn**: `adb screenrecord` is unavailable on some devices, and there the `screencap` loop is the only way to stream at all. `bgra` is unaffected (raw unencoded pixels are not something H.264 substitutes for). (#134, #138)

- Android `stream-video --format h264` is now carried in MPEG-TS instead of the bare Annex B `screenrecord` produces, matching the iOS surface — one `ffplay -f mpegts -probesize 32768 -i -` works on both platforms. An elementary stream carries no presentation timestamps, so a player guesses the frame rate (ffprobe reads it as 25 fps regardless of the real rate) and, when the device encodes faster, drains slower than sim-use fills: the lag grew without bound instead of settling, measured at 578 KB of queued video after 20 s and 1376 KB after 30 s of interaction, and observed in practice as a picture minutes behind the device. Frames are re-containered, never re-encoded — a new `MPEGTSMuxer` wraps them with a PTS taken from host arrival time (`screenrecord` is genuinely variable-frame-rate, so wall-clock arrival is the honest timeline). The player's queue now measures empty across a 30 s run. Program tables are emitted up front and re-announced every 100 ms, so a consumer attaching mid-stream can start decoding and a closed pipe is noticed even on a still screen; each picture carries its own clock reference, and a picture resuming after an idle stretch declares a transport discontinuity, since the timeline skipped real elapsed time rather than advancing through it; `--format h264` now reports a frame count in its summary because re-containering parses the stream. End-to-end latency measures ~0.6 s on an emulator, essentially all of it `screenrecord`'s own encode delay (0.58 s measured with sim-use out of the path).

  The stream's timeline advances by the real inter-frame gap but never by more than 0.2 s, which deliberately makes it *not* a reproduction of the wall clock. Capture is variable-frame-rate, so a still screen produces no frames; stamping the next picture with its true arrival time would open a hole in the timeline as long as the pause, and a player has to play through that hole before reaching the new picture — seen as a preview running minutes behind after the screen had been idle. Measured after the fix, time for the picture to catch up once interaction resumes: 0.45 s after 10 s idle, 0.51 s after 30 s, 1.20 s after 60 s; previously this tracked the idle duration. Reproducing the wall clock remains `record-video`'s job, and it keeps real arrival times for exactly that reason. (#135, #136)

- `--format h264`'s documented preview command is `ffplay -f mpegts -probesize 32768 -i -`. The previous `-probesize 32 -fflags nobuffer` never opened an Android stream: 32 bytes cannot identify the codec, and `-fflags nobuffer` starves the probe. `-probesize 32768` bounds the open by bytes, which is what matters on a variable-frame-rate source whose still screen sends only program tables — ffplay's default budget is measured in seconds of *media* and can take arbitrarily long in wall-clock terms to fill. `-analyzeduration 0` is deliberately not part of the command: zero selects ffmpeg's default analysis window rather than disabling it, and the open measured identically with and without it. A still Android screen produces no pictures at all, so the player opens once the device moves; iOS is constant-frame-rate and opens at once. (#136)

- iOS `record-video` and `stream-video` now share one set of H.264 encoder settings, built by `FBVideoStreamConfiguration.h264Capture(fps:quality:scale:transport:)`, so the two verbs cannot drift apart on how the picture is encoded. They still differ downstream in transport and sink — `record-video` into the shared `H264MuxingPipeline` → MP4 (the muxer Android has always used, and which was written for both), `stream-video` into stdout. Recording no longer goes through idb's separate in-process file writer. Output is equivalent: the MP4 stays a regular non-fragmented file that QuickTime, Finder and `GIFTranscoder` all read, `--fps` is still honoured as a constant rate, and the finalize path still survives a 100 ms-grace SIGTERM across repeated runs. Frame timestamps now come from host arrival time rather than the encoder's sample clock, which measures as ~6 ms of inter-frame jitter against the previous ~3 ms — both far inside a 33 ms frame at 30 fps. (#132, #133)

### Fixed

- iOS: with Device Hub open (Xcode 27), `batch --stdin`, `batch --file`, `type --stdin` and `paste --stdin` reported success but delivered nothing. These modes ran the command in the CLI process instead of the per-device daemon, because the daemon cannot read the caller's stdin. With Device Hub open, HID input goes through CoreDevice's `dtuhidd`, which takes about 0.4 s to set up each new connection before it reads any event. The CLI process exited first, and `dtuhidd` dropped the queued taps and keys. The client now reads the input and forwards it to the daemon inline, as `--step` arguments or as the text, so every event comes from the daemon's long-lived connection. For `type --file` and `paste --file`, a relative path now resolves against the caller's directory. Before, the path went to the daemon, which resolved it against its own directory. `SIM_USE_NO_DAEMON=1` still runs in-process and can drop input with Device Hub open. (#154)
- iOS: during an Xcode 27 resizable app session, `ui` no longer splices SpringBoard elements (home-screen widgets, the Dynamic Island, a 402x874 `Group`) into the app's tree, and no longer reports `Screen orientation could not be confirmed …` — or a confident `(landscape-right)` on an upright device — for a scene whose size merely differs from the device's. Both came from the accessibility point hit-test resolving on the main display, where SpringBoard is frontmost, while the tree fetch follows the app: the collapsed-children recovery walk adopted those hits as children, and the orientation calibrator read them as probe evidence. Under a session the tree is now returned as fetched, in identity calibration, with the `resizable_app_session` advisory explaining why. `ui --point` carries the same advisory, since its answer describes SpringBoard rather than the app. (#143, #150 — thanks @iXerol!)
- Android: a command that cannot reach the bridge even after reconnecting (wrong `SIM_USE_BRIDGE_HOST`, a firewall, an un-initialised device) now removes the forward it opened before reporting the error. No session had been saved for that forward, so nothing ever removed it and each failing attempt left one more forward on the adb server. (#147)
- Android: dropping a stale bridge forward now names the device (`adb -s <serial> forward --remove`). With more than one device on the adb server, the old command was rejected with "more than one device/emulator" and the error was swallowed, so every reconnect left another forward behind. (#147)
- iOS `stream-video --format h264` / `bgra`: a consumer that stops reading (ffplay paused, a wedged downstream tool) no longer makes Ctrl-C hang. The native stream went through idb's blocking file writer, which sat in `write(2)` on the encoder thread with `stopStreaming()` waiting behind it, so the command could not end short of SIGKILL. It now writes through the same interruptible stdout sink as Android — one that waits for room and checks cancellation between waits, and leaves the descriptor's flags untouched so the terminal (or stderr under `2>&1`) is never switched into non-blocking mode. A consumer that closes the pipe now ends the stream in an orderly way (stop messages, exit 0) instead of the process dying of SIGPIPE. (#138)
- The bundled skill preflight now reports a content warning instead of an unqualified pass when `ui` succeeds with a `remote_content_recovery` advisory or with an empty outline on a simulator, emulator or Android device. These reads still exit successfully. The warning points at a new *Missing app controls in the outline* pitfall, which covers the iOS simulator `ApplicationAccessibilityEnabled` launch-time setting. (#139, #145 — thanks @SunsetWan!)
- The bundled skill preflight now rejects an older `sim-use` CLI before device discovery and prints the Homebrew upgrade command, instead of misdiagnosing newly documented device types as disconnected. (#127 — thanks @BoWuGit!)
- iOS simulator selector-ambiguity errors now give advice an agent can act on. The `multipleMatches` hint de-duplicated labels, so three matches that share one label were reported as `matches (1)`; it now lists one `'label' [Type] #id` entry per match — the shape the physical-device backend already uses — and the count is the real number of matches, also past the 10-entry display cap. An ambiguous `--id` no longer recommends `--id`, and every ambiguity message now names `--element-type` / `--frame` to narrow the match. The `describe-ui` recovery tip and the missing outline-cache error recommend `--device` instead of the deprecated `--udid`. (#146)

@@ -7,8 +7,23 @@ and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0
 
 ## [Unreleased]
 
+### Added
+
+- iOS: the outline lists the **vertical bar** of an iOS 27.1 SDK app on the iPhone Duo as its own region, after the bands: `[Trailing  x>=396]` on the cover display (and on the inner display in landscape), `[Leading  x<=70]` when the cover is in landscape-right. The bar holds the back button (`#BackButton`, no label), trailing toolbar items, the tab bar and, where the app tree exposes them, status bar items; before, they were spread across `[Top]`, `[Content]` and `[Bottom]` between content rows. The region needs evidence — a back button or tab items stacked in a narrow edge strip that the app's wide content beside it stays clear of (an app header above the bar may start inside the strip) — so an iOS 27.0 SDK app, the inner display in portrait and every single-display simulator render as before (pinned by captured fixtures). `--json` entries carry `region.kind` `Leading` / `Trailing`. The Playground gained a `chrome-test` screen (navigation bar, toolbar, tab bar).
+- iOS: `sim-use ios rotate <orientation>` rotates any iOS simulator to an interface orientation — `portrait`, `landscape-left`, `landscape-right`, `portrait-upside-down`, the names the `ui` header prints — and reads the result back from CoreDevice. Single-display simulators rotate through a GSEvent sent to SpringBoard (verified on iOS 18.6, 26.5 and 27.0); the iPhone Duo through the orientation-picker HID report Device Hub sends, which is the only path its runtime obeys (`devicectl device orientation set` reports success there and changes nothing). When the frontmost app does not accept the orientation (a portrait-only app, SpringBoard on iPhone, `portrait-upside-down` on an iPhone-size screen) the command succeeds unconfirmed with an advisory naming the orientation the interface kept, rather than failing or claiming a rotation. A rotation clears the cached `ui` snapshot, so a stale `@N` cannot tap the old geometry.
+- iOS: `sim-use ios fold closed|open|half|<degrees>` folds and unfolds a foldable simulator (Xcode 27.1's iPhone Duo) with the hinge HID report that Device Hub's posture buttons send, then confirms the change by the display CoreDevice reports active — not by the backlight, which a locked device dims while the display stays active. `closed` and `open` fail if the expected display does not take over within `--timeout`; an intermediate angle reports the display it observed, because which display wins there depends on how the hinge got there. `sim-use ios fold` alone reports the posture. A fold clears the cached `ui` snapshot and wakes a locked device to its lock screen. The command refuses a simulator with one integrated display.
+- iOS: touch input, accessibility hit-tests and screenshots follow the display that hosts the app. On an unfolded iPhone Duo that is the inner display; during an Xcode 27 Resize Mode session it is the virtual `Resizable` display. sim-use reads the displays from `devicectl device info displays`, sends touches to that display's digitizer and its hit-tests to that display (a small idb patch adds both), and maps UI points through the display's rotation from CoreDevice instead of hit-test probes. `ui` reads the app's own tree, recovers collapsed groups again (the Settings sidebar on the inner display), sizes the outline to the display's interface (`951x669` in landscape instead of the panel's `669x951`) and tags the header with the display (`display LCD-1`, `display Resizable 560x874`; `--json`: a `display` object) — only off the main display, so single-display output is unchanged. `screenshot` captures that display. `record-video` and `stream-video` still capture only the main display and refuse with an explanation off it. An app whose scene is smaller than its display — an iOS 27.0 SDK app keeps out of the Duo's status bar strip, an older SDK app is centred on the inner display — is placed by a few hit-test probes, each offset confirmed by two elements, so taps land in every orientation (verified with LINE built against the iOS 27.0 SDK). Detection reads the display list once per daemon on a single-display simulator and at most every 2 s on a multi-display one; a `ui` whose accessibility root changed size re-reads it at once. `SIM_USE_DISPLAY_TOPOLOGY_CHECK=0` turns it off. The bundled skill's preflight now requires sim-use 0.16.0 or newer, because its iPhone Duo and rotation guidance uses these verbs. See `docs/ai/010-display-routing/000-plan.md`.
+
+### Changed
+
+- **iOS: explicit coordinates are now UI space by default** — the numbers `ui` prints. This covers `tap` / `long-press` `-x/-y` / `--point`, `swipe`, `touch` (the split `--down` / `--up` form too; each half is calibrated when it is sent), `multi-touch`, `paste --via-menu --target-x/--target-y`, the `gesture` pinch/rotate centre, radius and canvas, and the same verbs as `batch` steps. A coordinate read from the outline now lands where it was read on a rotated device, on a display-downscaled device (iPhone 12/13 mini: before, `tap -x 355 -y 758` missed a corner button the outline placed there), on the iPhone Duo inner display and in a Resize Mode session. **Breaking for scripts that pass device-native portrait points**: add `--coordinate-space native` to keep the old mapping. `--coordinate-space` (either value) is now rejected with an alias or a selector, and with a directional `gesture` preset; `multi-touch` and `gesture` gain the flag (accepted and ignored on Android, like the other verbs). The calibration reuses the last `ui` snapshot with a few hit-test probes and uses it only when the app's current root has the snapshot's size and the probes still find the snapshot's elements in place; otherwise it reads the tree once (~70 ms on a simple screen), which also notices a Resize Mode session that started, ended or was resized since. On iPhone 17 / iOS 27.0 the snapshot calibration takes 28–30 ms (`SIM_USE_PERF=1`) against ~75 ms for the tree. Calibration advisories now suggest `--coordinate-space native` instead of explicit coordinates. See `docs/ai/010-display-routing/000-plan.md` (S3).

+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+@preconcurrency import CoreSimulator
+import Darwin
+import FBSimulatorControl
+import Foundation
+import IOKit
+import SimUseCore
+import XPC
+
+/// A report from one of the controls of the simulator's virtual-machine
+/// provider. Device Hub's hinge slider and orientation picker send these,
+/// and `locationd` turns them into a hinge angle or a device orientation.
+///
+/// Wire format and payload keys match upstream idb
+/// (`IndigoVendorDefinedEvent.virtualMachineControl`), so the idb migration
+/// can replace this file without a behaviour change. Work record:
+/// docs/ai/010-display-routing/000-plan.md (E1, E2).
+public enum VirtualMachineControl: Equatable, Sendable {
+    /// 0 (closed) … 180 (flat), degrees.
+    case hinge(degrees: Double)
+    /// A device orientation in the provider's vocabulary.
+    case orientation(VirtualMachineOrientation)
+
+    var source: String {
+        switch self {
+        case .hinge: return "hinge-slider-control"
+        case .orientation: return "orientation-picker-control"
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The dictionary the provider reads.
+    var payload: [String: Any] {
+        switch self {
+        case .hinge(let degrees):
+            return ["provider": Self.provider, "source": source, "type": "range", "value": degrees]
+        case .orientation(let orientation):
+            return ["provider": Self.provider, "source": source, "type": "enum", "value": orientation.rawValue]
+        }
+    }
+
+    static let provider = "com.apple.Virtualization.VirtualMachines"
+    static let usagePage: UInt64 = 0xFF61
+    static let usage: UInt64 = 0x5B
+
+    /// The payload as an IOKit binary property list (`OSSerializeBinary`),
+    /// the format the vendor report carries.
+    func serializedPayload() throws -> Data {
+        guard let serialized = IOCFSerialize(payload as CFDictionary, CFOptionFlags(kIOCFSerializeToBinary)) else {
+            throw CLIError(errorDescription: "Could not serialise the \(source) report.")
+        }
+        return serialized as Data
+    }
+}
+
+/// Device orientations the orientation picker accepts. Device convention:
+/// `landscapeLeft` here turns the interface to sim-use's `landscape-right`.
+public enum VirtualMachineOrientation: String, Equatable, Sendable {
+    case portrait
+    case portraitUpsideDown = "pud"
+    case landscapeLeft = "landscape-left"
+    case landscapeRight = "landscape-right"
+}
+
+/// Sends vendor-defined HID reports to the simulator's `dtuhidd` over the
+/// host-to-guest XPC service `com.apple.coredevice.feature.remote.hid.vendordefined`,
+/// the path Device Hub uses. Device Hub does not need to be running.
+///
+/// One connection per send: hinge and orientation changes are rare and
+/// confirmed by reading CoreDevice state back, and a dead cached
+/// connection after a reboot would fail silently.
+public enum VendorDefinedHID {
+    public static let serviceName = "com.apple.coredevice.feature.remote.hid.vendordefined"
+
+    /// How long the connection stays open after the barrier reply, so the
+    /// guest picks the report up before dtuhidd removes the connection's
+    /// services (a new peer's services take ~0.8 s to appear — plan E5).
+    static let settleNanos: UInt64 = 1_000_000_000
+
+    public static func send(_ control: VirtualMachineControl, to simulator: FBSimulator, logger: SimUseLogger) async throws {
+        let data = try control.serializedPayload()
+        let connection = try connect(to: simulator)
+        defer { xpc_connection_cancel(connection) }
+
+        let payload = xpc_dictionary_create(nil, nil, 0)
+        xpc_dictionary_set_uint64(payload, "usagePage", VirtualMachineControl.usagePage)
+        xpc_dictionary_set_uint64(payload, "usage", VirtualMachineControl.usage)
+        xpc_dictionary_set_uint64(payload, "version", 0)
+        data.withUnsafeBytes { buffer in
+            xpc_dictionary_set_data(payload, "data", buffer.baseAddress!, buffer.count)
+        }
+        let message = xpc_dictionary_create(nil, nil, 0)
+        xpc_dictionary_set_string(message, "messageType", "IndigoVendorDefinedEvent")
+        xpc_dictionary_set_bool(message, "isBarrier", false)
+        xpc_dictionary_set_string(message, "featureIdentifier", serviceName)
+        xpc_dictionary_set_value(message, "payload", payload)
+        logger.info().log("Sending \(control.source) report to \(serviceName)")
+        xpc_connection_send_message(connection, message)
+
+        // dtuhidd answers a barrier once everything sent before it has
+        // been dispatched.
+        let barrier = xpc_dictionary_create(nil, nil, 0)
+        xpc_dictionary_set_bool(barrier, "isBarrier", true)
+        let reply: xpc_object_t = await withCheckedContinuation { continuation in
+            xpc_connection_send_message_with_reply(connection, barrier, nil) { reply in
+                continuation.resume(returning: reply)
+            }
+        }
+        if xpc_get_type(reply) == XPC_TYPE_ERROR {
+            let description = xpc_dictionary_get_string(reply, XPC_ERROR_KEY_DESCRIPTION).map { String(cString: $0) } ?? "unknown error"
+            throw CLIError(errorDescription: "dtuhidd did not acknowledge the \(control.source) report: \(description)")
+        }
+        try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: settleNanos)
+    }
+
+    // MARK: Connection
+
+    private typealias EndpointFromMachPortFn = @convention(c) (mach_port_t, UInt64, UInt64) -> xpc_object_t?
+    private typealias ConnectionFromEndpointFn = @convention(c) (xpc_object_t) -> xpc_connection_t?
+    private typealias EnableSim2HostFn = @convention(c) (xpc_connection_t) -> Void
+
+    private static func connect(to simulator: FBSimulator) throws -> xpc_connection_t {
+        guard let handle = dlopen(nil, RTLD_NOW),
+              let endpointFromPort = symbol(handle, "xpc_endpoint_create_mach_port_4sim", as: EndpointFromMachPortFn.self),
+              let connectionFromEndpoint = symbol(handle, "xpc_connection_create_from_endpoint", as: ConnectionFromEndpointFn.self),
+              let enableSim2Host = symbol(handle, "xpc_connection_enable_sim2host_4sim", as: EnableSim2HostFn.self)
+        else {
+            throw CLIError(errorDescription: "The host-to-simulator XPC symbols are not available on this macOS.")
+        }
+
+        let port = try lookup(serviceName, on: simulator)
+        guard let endpoint = endpointFromPort(port, 0, 0),
+              let connection = connectionFromEndpoint(endpoint)
+        else {
+            throw CLIError(errorDescription: "Could not open an XPC connection to \(serviceName) in simulator \(simulator.udid).")
+        }
+        // Without this the daemon sees the peer but never the payload.
+        enableSim2Host(connection)
+        xpc_connection_set_event_handler(connection) { _ in }
+        xpc_connection_resume(connection)
+        return connection
+    }
+
+    private static func lookup(_ service: String, on simulator: FBSimulator) throws -> mach_port_t {
+        var error: NSError?
+        let port = simulator.device.lookup(service, error: &error)
+        guard port != MACH_PORT_NULL else {
+            let reason = error?.localizedDescription ?? "the service is not registered"
+            throw CLIError(errorDescription: "Simulator \(simulator.udid) has no \(service) service (\(reason)). It needs an Xcode 27 runtime with dtuhidd.")
+        }
+        return port
+    }
+
+    private static func symbol<T>(_ handle: UnsafeMutableRawPointer, _ name: String, as type: T.Type) -> T? {
+        guard let sym = dlsym(handle, name) else { return nil }
+        return unsafeBitCast(sym, to: type)
+    }
+}

+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+import Foundation
+
+/// One finished `xcrun devicectl … --json-output -` run. The probes that
+/// read CoreDevice state about a simulator (`ResizableAppSessionProbe`,
+/// `SimulatorDisplayTopologyProbe`) classify this value, so every shape
+/// they handle can be pinned in tests without CoreDevice.
+public struct DevicectlQueryOutput: Sendable {
+    public let terminationStatus: Int32
+    public let stdout: Data
+    public let stderr: Data
+
+    public init(terminationStatus: Int32, stdout: Data, stderr: Data) {
+        self.terminationStatus = terminationStatus
+        self.stdout = stdout
+        self.stderr = stderr
+    }
+
+    /// devicectl writes its JSON document on success *and* on failure, so
+    /// callers trust the document rather than the exit status.
+    public var document: [String: Any]? {
+        (try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: stdout)) as? [String: Any]
+    }
+
+    /// stderr then stdout, trimmed — for "unknown subcommand" detection
+    /// and error messages.
+    public var combinedText: String {
+        let text = (String(data: stderr, encoding: .utf8) ?? "") + (String(data: stdout, encoding: .utf8) ?? "")
+        return text.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
+    }
+
+    /// True when devicectl rejected the subcommand itself — an older Xcode
+    /// that does not know it. Callers remember this for the process life.
+    public var isUnknownSubcommand: Bool {
+        let text = combinedText
+        return text.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains("unrecognized subcommand")
+            || text.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains("unknown subcommand")
+            || text.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains("unexpected argument")
+    }
+
+    /// `"<domain> error <code>: <description>"` for a devicectl error
+    /// document, or nil when the document carries no `error`.
+    public var errorSummary: (code: Int?, summary: String)? {
+        guard let error = document?["error"] as? [String: Any] else { return nil }
+        let code = DevicectlQuery.number(error["code"]).map { Int($0) }
+        let description = ((error["userInfo"] as? [String: Any])?["NSLocalizedDescription"] as? [String: Any])?["string"] as? String
+        let domain = (error["domain"] as? String) ?? "CoreDevice"
+        return (code, "\(domain) error \(code.map(String.init) ?? "?")\(description.map { ": \($0)" } ?? "")")
+    }
+}
+
+/// Runs devicectl (through `xcrun`, so the selected Xcode's devicectl) and
+/// captures both streams.
+public enum DevicectlQuery {
+    /// Spawns the process and waits for it. Returns nil only when the
+    /// process cannot be spawned; `spawnError` receives the reason.
+    /// `executablePath` is injectable so tests can drive the drain against
+    /// `/bin/sh`; production uses `xcrun`.
+    public static func run(
+        arguments: [String],
+        executablePath: String = "/usr/bin/xcrun",
+        spawnError: ((String) -> Void)? = nil
+    ) -> DevicectlQueryOutput? {
+        let process = Process()
+        process.executableURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: executablePath)
+        process.arguments = arguments
+
+        let stdout = Pipe()
+        let stderr = Pipe()
+        process.standardOutput = stdout
+        process.standardError = stderr
+
+        // Drain both pipes while the child runs so neither can fill the
+        // ~64 KB pipe buffer and deadlock `waitUntilExit()`. Same drain as
+        // `SimctlDeviceLister.runSimctl` and `Devicectl.run`.
+        let bufferLock = NSLock()
+        var outBuffer = Data()
+        var errBuffer = Data()
+        stdout.fileHandleForReading.readabilityHandler = { handle in
+            let chunk = handle.availableData
+            guard !chunk.isEmpty else { return }
+            bufferLock.lock(); outBuffer.append(chunk); bufferLock.unlock()
+        }
+        stderr.fileHandleForReading.readabilityHandler = { handle in
+            let chunk = handle.availableData
+            guard !chunk.isEmpty else { return }
+            bufferLock.lock(); errBuffer.append(chunk); bufferLock.unlock()
+        }
+
+        do {
+            try process.run()
+        } catch {
+            spawnError?("could not spawn xcrun devicectl: \(error.localizedDescription)")
+            return nil
+        }
+        process.waitUntilExit()
+
+        stdout.fileHandleForReading.readabilityHandler = nil
+        stderr.fileHandleForReading.readabilityHandler = nil
+        bufferLock.lock()
+        outBuffer.append(stdout.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile())
+        errBuffer.append(stderr.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile())
+        bufferLock.unlock()
+
+        return DevicectlQueryOutput(terminationStatus: process.terminationStatus, stdout: outBuffer, stderr: errBuffer)
+    }
+
+    static func number(_ value: Any?) -> Double? {
+        if let d = value as? Double { return d }
+        if let n = value as? NSNumber { return n.doubleValue }
+        return nil
+    }
+}

+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+import FBSimulatorControl
+import Foundation
+import SimUseCore
+
+/// Sends hinge and orientation changes and confirms them by reading
+/// CoreDevice back. The signal is the display `active` flag and the
+/// display rotation, never the backlight (plan E19, E20).
+public enum PostureController {
+    public struct FoldOutcome: Codable, Equatable, Sendable {
+        public let requested: String
+        public let hingeAngle: Double
+        /// True when the expected display became active. Always true for an
+        /// intermediate angle, which has no expectation (plan E21).
+        public let confirmed: Bool
+        public let posture: PostureReport
+    }
+
+    public struct RotateOutcome: Codable, Equatable, Sendable {
+        public let requested: String
+        /// The device orientation sent last (device convention).
+        public let deviceOrientation: String
+        /// The interface orientation the routing display shows afterwards.
+        public let orientation: String?
+        public let confirmed: Bool
+        public let posture: PostureReport?
+    }
+
+    static let pollInterval: UInt64 = 250_000_000
+    /// How long a rotation read-back other than the wanted one must wait
+    /// before it counts as the answer.
+    static let unexpectedReportGrace: TimeInterval = 1.5
+
+    // MARK: Fold
+
+    public static func fold(
+        udid: String,
+        target: FoldTarget,
+        timeout: TimeInterval,
+        logger: SimUseLogger,
+        topologyMonitor: SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor = .shared,
+        sessionMonitor: ResizableAppSessionMonitor = .shared
+    ) async throws -> FoldOutcome {
+        let topology = try await requireTopology(udid: udid, monitor: topologyMonitor)
+        guard topology.isMultiDisplay else {
+            throw CLIError(errorDescription: "Simulator \(udid) has \(topology.integratedDisplays.count) integrated display; `ios fold` applies to foldable simulators such as iPhone Duo.")
+        }
+
+        let session = try await HIDInteractor.makeSession(for: udid, logger: logger)
+        try await VendorDefinedHID.send(.hinge(degrees: target.degrees), to: session.simulator, logger: logger)
+        OutlineCache.invalidate(udid: udid)
+
+        let expectation = target.expectation
+        let settled = await waitForTopology(udid: udid, timeout: timeout, monitor: topologyMonitor) { previous, current in
+            guard expectation.isMet(by: current) else { return false }
+            // Without an expectation, wait for two equal reads so a
+            // display switch still in flight is not reported.
+            if expectation == .observeOnly {
+                return previous?.activeIntegrated?.uniqueID == current.activeIntegrated?.uniqueID
+            }
+            return true
+        }
+        let final = settled.topology ?? topology
+        let confirmed = settled.met
+        let sessionState = await postureChanged(udid: udid, topologyMonitor: topologyMonitor, sessionMonitor: sessionMonitor)
+        let outcome = FoldOutcome(
+            requested: target.description,
+            hingeAngle: target.degrees,
+            confirmed: confirmed,
+            posture: PostureReport(topology: final, session: sessionState)
+        )
+        guard confirmed else {
+            let expected = expectation == .primaryActive ? "the primary display" : "a non-primary integrated display"
+            throw CLIError(errorDescription: "Sent hinge \(ResizableAppSession.format(target.degrees))° to simulator \(udid), but \(expected) did not become active within \(ResizableAppSession.format(timeout)) s (\(outcome.posture.summary)).")
+        }
+        return outcome
+    }
+
+    // MARK: Rotate
+
+    public static func rotate(
+        udid: String,
+        target: DisplayOrientation,
+        timeout: TimeInterval,
+        logger: SimUseLogger,
+        topologyMonitor: SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor = .shared,
+        sessionMonitor: ResizableAppSessionMonitor = .shared
+    ) async throws -> (outcome: RotateOutcome, advisory: CommandAdvisory?) {
+        try await assertNoResizeSession(udid: udid, sessionMonitor: sessionMonitor)
+
+        let before = await topologyMonitor.state(for: udid, fresh: true).topology
+        let session = try await HIDInteractor.makeSession(for: udid, logger: logger)
+        let multiDisplay = before?.isMultiDisplay ?? false
+        let display = before.flatMap { $0.activeIntegrated ?? $0.primary }
+
+        let wanted = RotationPlanner.deviceOrientation(for: target)
+        var offset = RotationPlanner.initialTransportOffset(display: multiDisplay ? display : nil)
+        var sent = RotationPlanner.sendValue(for: wanted, transportOffset: offset)
+        try await send(sent, multiDisplay: multiDisplay, session: session, logger: logger)
+        OutlineCache.invalidate(udid: udid)
+
+        var after = await waitForRotation(udid: udid, wanted: wanted, timeout: timeout, monitor: topologyMonitor)
+        // The transport offset of a secondary display is a guess. When the
+        // device turned, but to the wrong side, the read-back gives the
+        // real offset and one corrected send lands. A report that did not
+        // change at all teaches nothing: the frontmost app or the display
+        // does not accept the orientation (an iPhone-size screen refuses
+        // portrait-upside-down; a portrait-only app keeps portrait).
+        if let reported = after?.deviceOrientation, reported != wanted.rawValue,
+           reported != before?.deviceOrientation,
+           let learned = RotationPlanner.learnedTransportOffset(sent: sent, reported: reported), learned != offset
+        {
+            logger.info().log("Orientation report \(sent.rawValue) read back as \(reported); correcting the transport offset from \(offset) to \(learned)")
+            offset = learned
+            sent = RotationPlanner.sendValue(for: wanted, transportOffset: offset)
+            try await send(sent, multiDisplay: multiDisplay, session: session, logger: logger)
+            after = await waitForRotation(udid: udid, wanted: wanted, timeout: timeout, monitor: topologyMonitor)
+        }
+        _ = await postureChanged(udid: udid, topologyMonitor: topologyMonitor, sessionMonitor: sessionMonitor)
+
+        guard let after else {
+            // No CoreDevice read-back (older devicectl): the change was
+            // sent but cannot be confirmed.
+            let outcome = RotateOutcome(requested: target.rawValue, deviceOrientation: wanted.rawValue, orientation: nil, confirmed: false, posture: nil)
+            return (outcome, CommandAdvisory(
+                kind: .orientationCalibrationFallback,
+                message: "Sent device orientation \(wanted.rawValue), but CoreDevice could not report the result on this Xcode; run `describe-ui` to see the interface orientation."
+            ))
+        }
+
+        let reached = (after.activeIntegrated ?? after.primary)?.rotation.interfaceOrientation
+        let outcome = RotateOutcome(
+            requested: target.rawValue,
+            deviceOrientation: wanted.rawValue,
+            orientation: reached?.rawValue,
+            confirmed: reached == target,
+            posture: PostureReport(topology: after, session: nil)
+        )
+        guard reached == target else {
+            return (outcome, CommandAdvisory(
+                kind: .orientationCalibrationFallback,
+                message: "The interface stayed \(reached?.rawValue ?? "unknown"): the frontmost app or the display does not accept \(target.rawValue) " +
+                    "(for example a portrait-only app, SpringBoard on iPhone, or portrait-upside-down on an iPhone-size screen). " +
+                    "CoreDevice reports device orientation \(after.deviceOrientation ?? "unknown")."
+            ))
+        }
+        return (outcome, nil)
+    }
+
+    /// Single-display simulators rotate through the Purple GSEvent path
+    /// that the HID connection already carries; a multi-display simulator
+    /// only reacts to the orientation picker report (plan E10–E13), the
+    /// same split upstream idb makes on "runtime reports device motion".
+    static func send(
+        _ orientation: DeviceOrientationValue,
+        multiDisplay: Bool,
+        session: HIDInteractor.Session,
+        logger: SimUseLogger
+    ) async throws {
+        if multiDisplay {
+            try await VendorDefinedHID.send(.orientation(orientation.virtualMachineValue), to: session.simulator, logger: logger)
+        } else {
+            try await HIDInteractor.performHIDEvent(.deviceOrientation(orientation.purpleOrientation), in: session, logger: logger)
+        }
+    }
+
+    // MARK: Cached state
+
+    /// After a fold or a rotation: the routing state the daemon caches is
+    /// stale (unfolding ends a Resize Mode session, R157-01). Returns the
+    /// session state now.
+    static func postureChanged(
+        udid: String,
+        topologyMonitor: SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor,
+        sessionMonitor: ResizableAppSessionMonitor
+    ) async -> ResizableAppSession? {
+        await topologyMonitor.invalidate(udid: udid)
+        await sessionMonitor.invalidate(udid: udid)
+        return await sessionMonitor.state(for: udid).session
+    }
+
+    /// Resize Mode sessions are portrait-only. Checked against CoreDevice,
+    /// not the cache: a fold or another tool may have ended the session
+    /// inside the cache window.
+    static func assertNoResizeSession(udid: String, sessionMonitor: ResizableAppSessionMonitor) async throws {
+        await sessionMonitor.invalidate(udid: udid)
+        if case .active(let resizable) = await sessionMonitor.state(for: udid) {
+            throw CLIError(errorDescription: "A resizable app session (Xcode 27 Resize Mode, \(resizable.preferredSizeDescription)) is active on simulator \(udid). Sessions are portrait-only; end the session before rotating.")
+        }
+    }
+
+    // MARK: Polling
+
+    static func requireTopology(udid: String, monitor: SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor) async throws -> SimulatorDisplayTopology {
+        switch await monitor.state(for: udid, fresh: true) {
+        case .available(let topology):
+            return topology
+        case .unavailable(let reason):
+            throw CLIError(errorDescription: "Could not read the displays of simulator \(udid) from CoreDevice (\(reason)). `ios fold` needs `xcrun devicectl` from Xcode 26.6 or later.")
+        }
+    }
+
+    static func waitForTopology(
+        udid: String,
+        timeout: TimeInterval,
+        monitor: SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor,
+        isSettled: (SimulatorDisplayTopology?, SimulatorDisplayTopology) -> Bool
+    ) async -> (topology: SimulatorDisplayTopology?, met: Bool) {
+        let deadline = Date().addingTimeInterval(timeout)
+        var previous: SimulatorDisplayTopology?
+        var last: SimulatorDisplayTopology?
+        repeat {
+            if let topology = await monitor.state(for: udid, fresh: true).topology {
+                if isSettled(previous, topology) { return (topology, true) }
+                previous = topology
+                last = topology
+            }
+            try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: pollInterval)
+        } while Date() < deadline
+        return (last, false)
+    }
+
+    /// Waits for the device to report `wanted` and the active display's
+    /// rotation to hold for two reads. Returns the last read when the
+    /// device settles elsewhere (so the caller can learn from it), nil when
+    /// CoreDevice cannot answer.
+    static func waitForRotation(
+        udid: String,
+        wanted: DeviceOrientationValue,
+        timeout: TimeInterval,
+        monitor: SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor
+    ) async -> SimulatorDisplayTopology? {
+        let start = Date()
+        let result = await waitForTopology(udid: udid, timeout: timeout, monitor: monitor) { previous, current in
+            // Settled when two reads agree on the reported orientation and
+            // on the rotation. A report other than `wanted` that holds is
+            // an answer too — a wrong transport offset, or a device that
+            // refused — but only after `unexpectedReportGrace`, because the
+            // first reads can still show the orientation from before.
+            guard let previous, let reported = current.deviceOrientation,
+                  previous.deviceOrientation == reported,
+                  (previous.activeIntegrated ?? previous.primary)?.rotation == (current.activeIntegrated ?? current.primary)?.rotation
+            else { return false }
+            return reported == wanted.rawValue || Date().timeIntervalSince(start) >= unexpectedReportGrace
+        }
+        return result.topology
+    }
+}
+
+extension DeviceOrientationValue {
+    /// The Purple GSEvent value for this device orientation. Purple numbers
+    /// landscape in interface style, so device left and right swap
+    /// (upstream idb `physicalPurpleOrientation`).
+    var purpleOrientation: FBSimulatorHIDDeviceOrientation {
+        switch self {
+        case .portrait: return .portrait
+        case .portraitUpsideDown: return .portraitUpsideDown
+        case .landscapeLeft: return .landscapeRight
+        case .landscapeRight: return .landscapeLeft
+        }
+    }
+}

+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+import FBSimulatorControl
+import Foundation
+import SimUseCore
+
+// MARK: - Routing display
+
+/// The display that hosts the frontmost app, which is the display every
+/// input, accessibility and capture primitive has to address.
+///
+/// | State | Routing display |
+/// | --- | --- |
+/// | Resize Mode session active | the virtual `Resizable` display |
+/// | more than one integrated display, a non-primary one active | that display (iPhone Duo inner screen) |
+/// | otherwise | the main display — the historical, unchanged path |
+///
+/// Work record: docs/ai/010-display-routing/000-plan.md.
+public enum RoutingDisplay: Equatable, Sendable {
+    case main
+    /// A non-primary integrated display hosts the interface (an unfolded
+    /// iPhone Duo).
+    case secondary(SimulatorDisplay)
+    /// A Resize Mode session (issue #143). The display entry is nil when
+    /// the topology could not be read.
+    case resizable(ResizableAppSession, SimulatorDisplay?)
+
+    public var isMain: Bool { self == .main }
+
+    public var displayName: String? {
+        switch self {
+        case .main: return nil
+        case .secondary(let display): return display.name
+        case .resizable(let session, let display): return display?.name ?? session.displayName
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The CoreDevice display UUID to capture, nil for the main display.
+    public var captureUniqueID: String? {
+        switch self {
+        case .main: return nil
+        case .secondary(let display): return display.uniqueID
+        case .resizable(let session, _): return session.displayUniqueID
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The interface orientation of a secondary display, from CoreDevice.
+    /// A Resize Mode scene is always upright (sessions refuse to start
+    /// rotated — plan E17).
+    public var interfaceOrientation: DisplayOrientation? {
+        switch self {
+        case .main: return nil
+        case .secondary(let display): return display.rotation.interfaceOrientation
+        case .resizable: return .portrait
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The unrotated panel of a secondary display in points.
+    public var panelPoints: NativePortraitSize? {
+        if case .secondary(let display) = self { return display.panelPoints }
+        return nil
+    }
+
+    /// Serialised into `describe-ui --json` only off the main display.
+    public var info: RoutingDisplayInfo? {
+        switch self {
+        case .main:
+            return nil
+        case .secondary(let display):
+            return RoutingDisplayInfo(
+                name: display.name,
+                id: Int(display.displayID),
+                kind: display.kind.label,
+                primary: display.isPrimary,
+                rotation: display.rotation.rawValue,
+                resizableSession: nil
+            )
+        case .resizable(let session, let display):
+            return RoutingDisplayInfo(
+                name: display?.name ?? session.displayName,
+                id: display.map { Int($0.displayID) },
+                kind: display?.kind.label ?? SimulatorDisplay.Kind.virtual.label,
+                primary: false,
+                rotation: SimulatorDisplayRotation.rot0.rawValue,
+                resizableSession: .init(preferredWidth: session.preferredWidth, preferredHeight: session.preferredHeight)
+            )
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Appended to the outline `App:` header off the main display, so the
+    /// common single-display header stays byte-identical.
+    public var headerTag: String? {
+        switch self {
+        case .main:
+            return nil
+        case .secondary(let display):
+            return "display \(display.name)"
+        case .resizable(let session, let display):
+            return "display \(display?.name ?? session.displayName) \(session.preferredSizeDescription)"
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+// MARK: - Addressing a routing display
+
+extension RoutingDisplay {
+    /// The AX translator display the hit-test and the tree fetch address:
+    /// the CoreDevice display id (plan E6, E7, E15). 0 is the main display.
+    public var accessibilityDisplayID: UInt32 {
+        switch self {
+        case .main: return 0
+        case .secondary(let display): return display.displayID
+        case .resizable(_, let display): return display?.displayID ?? 0
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// The UI → HID / hit-test transform off the main display, known from
+    /// CoreDevice without hit-test probes. A secondary display maps through
+    /// its rotation onto its unrotated panel (plan E4). A Resize Mode scene
+    /// is upright and sits at the canvas origin, so its points pass through
+    /// (E14); `sceneSize` is its size in points, when known. Nil on the
+    /// main display, which keeps the self-calibration.
+    public func fixedCalibration(sceneSize: CGSize?) -> OrientationCalibration? {
+        switch self {
+        case .main:
+            return nil
+        case .secondary(let display):
+            return OrientationCalibration(
+                orientation: display.rotation.interfaceOrientation,
+                native: display.panelPoints,
+                probesUsed: 0,
+                advisory: nil
+            )
+        case .resizable:
+            return .identity(native: sceneSize.map { NativePortraitSize(width: Double($0.width), height: Double($0.height)) })
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Where touch input goes. Nil on the main display (the historical
+    /// path). A Resize Mode session normalizes scene points against the
+    /// whole `Resizable` canvas in pixels (E14, E18); a secondary display
+    /// against its panel.
+    public func hidRoute() throws -> FBSimulatorHIDDisplayRoute? {
+        switch self {
+        case .main:
+            return nil
+        case .secondary(let display):
+            return Self.route(for: display)
+        case .resizable(let session, let display):
+            guard let display else {

+public enum RoutingDisplayResolver {

+        topology: SimulatorDisplayTopologyState

+            return .resizable(resizable, topology.topology?.display(uniqueID: resizable.displayUniqueID))
+        }

+public enum RoutingDisplayGuard {
+    /// Call after global setup in every verb that dispatches touch HID.
+    /// Touch input reaches the display that hosts the app, so this only
+    /// fails when that display cannot be addressed: a Resize Mode session
+    /// whose display CoreDevice did not list. The route itself is applied
+    /// per event by `HIDInteractor.routeTouches`. `verb` is kept for the log.
+    public static func assertTouchInputReachesApp(
+        udid: String,
+        verb: String,
+        logger: SimUseLogger,
+        sessionMonitor: ResizableAppSessionMonitor = .shared,
+        topologyMonitor: SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor = .shared
+    ) async throws {
+        let routing = await RoutingDisplayResolver.current(udid: udid, sessionMonitor: sessionMonitor, topologyMonitor: topologyMonitor)
+        if let name = routing.displayName {
+            logger.info().log("\(verb): the app is on display \(name); touch input is routed there")
+        }
+        _ = try routing.hidRoute()
+    }
+
+    /// Call after global setup in every verb that captures the main
+    /// framebuffer without redirection (`record-video`, `stream-video`),
+    /// before any output file is created or byte is emitted.
+    public static func assertCaptureReachesApp(
+        udid: String,
+        verb: String,
+        logger: SimUseLogger,
+        sessionMonitor: ResizableAppSessionMonitor = .shared,
+        topologyMonitor: SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor = .shared
+    ) async throws {
+        switch await RoutingDisplayResolver.current(udid: udid, sessionMonitor: sessionMonitor, topologyMonitor: topologyMonitor) {

+        case .resizable(let session, _):
+            logger.info().log("Resizable app session active on \(udid) (\(session.displayName) \(session.preferredSizeDescription)); refusing \(verb) (main-display capture only)")

+            throw SecondaryDisplayCaptureError(verb: verb, udid: udid, display: display)
+        }
+    }

+// MARK: - Probe (devicectl)
+
+/// Reads the display list through `devicectl device info displays` (~0.1 s,
+/// plan E9). Works with the devicectl of Xcode 26.6, 27.0 and 27.1.
+public enum SimulatorDisplayTopologyProbe {
+    /// Pinned by test. Same shape as `ResizableAppSessionProbe.arguments`.
+    public static func arguments(udid: String) -> [String] {
+        [
+            "devicectl", "device", "info", "displays",
+            "--device", udid,
+            "--json-output", "-",
+            "--timeout", "5",
+            "--quiet",
+        ]
+    }
+
+    public static func classify(_ output: DevicectlQueryOutput) -> SimulatorDisplayTopologyState {
+        if let result = output.document?["result"] as? [String: Any],
+           let rawDisplays = result["displays"] as? [[String: Any]]
+        {
+            let displays = rawDisplays.compactMap(display(from:))
+            guard !displays.isEmpty else {
+                return .unavailable(reason: "devicectl listed no readable display")
+            }
+            let orientation = (result["orientation"] as? [String: Any])?["currentDeviceOrientation"] as? String
+            return .available(SimulatorDisplayTopology(displays: displays, deviceOrientation: orientation))
+        }
+        if let error = output.errorSummary {
+            return .unavailable(reason: error.summary)
+        }
+        if output.isUnknownSubcommand {
+            return .unavailable(reason: "devicectl has no `device info displays` subcommand")
+        }
+        let trimmed = output.combinedText
+        return .unavailable(reason: "devicectl exited \(output.terminationStatus)\(trimmed.isEmpty ? "" : ": \(trimmed.prefix(300))")")
+    }
+
+    public static func run(udid: String, executablePath: String = "/usr/bin/xcrun") -> SimulatorDisplayTopologyState {
+        var spawnFailure = "could not spawn xcrun devicectl"
+        guard let output = DevicectlQuery.run(
+            arguments: arguments(udid: udid),
+            executablePath: executablePath,
+            spawnError: { spawnFailure = $0 }
+        ) else {
+            return .unavailable(reason: spawnFailure)
+        }
+        return classify(output)
+    }
+
+    /// One display entry. Entries without an id or a size are dropped
+    /// rather than guessed.
+    static func display(from raw: [String: Any]) -> SimulatorDisplay? {
+        guard let id = DevicectlQuery.number(raw["displayId"]), id >= 0, id <= Double(UInt32.max) else { return nil }
+        let name = (raw["name"] as? String) ?? "display \(Int(id))"
+        // Runtimes before iOS 27 report no `uniqueId` (verified on iOS 18.6
+        // and 26.5); the name identifies the display there, and `simctl io
+        // --display` accepts it too.
+        let uniqueID = (raw["uniqueId"] as? String).flatMap { $0.isEmpty ? nil : $0 } ?? name
+
+        // `bounds` is `[[x, y], [w, h]]`; `nativeSize` is `[w, h]`. Both
+        // carry the unrotated panel in pixels.
+        var size: (Double, Double)?
+        if let bounds = raw["bounds"] as? [[Any]], bounds.count == 2, bounds[1].count == 2,
+           let w = DevicectlQuery.number(bounds[1][0]), let h = DevicectlQuery.number(bounds[1][1]) {
+            size = (w, h)
+        } else if let native = raw["nativeSize"] as? [Any], native.count == 2,
+                  let w = DevicectlQuery.number(native[0]), let h = DevicectlQuery.number(native[1]) {
+            size = (w, h)
+        }
+        guard let (width, height) = size else { return nil }
+
+        let kind: SimulatorDisplay.Kind
+        if let type = raw["type"] as? [String: Any], let key = type.keys.sorted().first {
+            switch key {
+            case "integrated": kind = .integrated
+            case "virtual": kind = .virtual
+            default: kind = .other(key)
+            }
+        } else {
+            kind = .other("unknown")
+        }
+
+        return SimulatorDisplay(
+            displayID: UInt32(id),
+            uniqueID: uniqueID,
+            name: name,
+            kind: kind,
+            isPrimary: (raw["primary"] as? Bool) ?? false,
+            isActive: (raw["active"] as? Bool) ?? false,
+            backlightState: raw["backlightState"] as? String,
+            rotation: (raw["currentOrientation"] as? String).flatMap(SimulatorDisplayRotation.init(rawValue:)) ?? .rot0,
+            pixelWidth: width,
+            pixelHeight: height,
+            pointScale: DevicectlQuery.number(raw["pointScale"]) ?? 0
+        )
+    }
+}

+// MARK: - Monitor (cache)
+
+/// Per-UDID cache in front of `SimulatorDisplayTopologyProbe`, kept in the
+/// per-UDID daemon.
+///
+/// The display set of a device type never changes, so a device seen with
+/// one integrated display keeps its first answer for the life of the
+/// process: traditional iPhones pay one ~0.1 s probe per daemon, not one per
+/// command. A multi-display device can change its active display at any
+/// time (fold, hinge, lock), so its answer lives for `ttl` and `fold` /
+/// `rotate` invalidate it. `fresh: true` bypasses the cache for callers
+/// that need the current rotation.
+public actor SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor {
+    public typealias Probe = @Sendable (String) -> SimulatorDisplayTopologyState
+
+    public static let shared = SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor()
+
+    public static let defaultTTL: TimeInterval = 2
+    public static let disableEnvironmentKey = "SIM_USE_DISPLAY_TOPOLOGY_CHECK"
+
+    /// The size of an accessibility root, compared by value.
+    public struct RootSize: Equatable, Sendable {
+        public let width: Double
+        public let height: Double
+
+        public init(width: Double, height: Double) {
+            self.width = width
+            self.height = height
+        }
+    }
+
+    private struct CacheEntry {
+        let state: SimulatorDisplayTopologyState
+        let checkedAt: Date
+        /// The AX root size the probe was made with, nil when none was offered.
+        let rootSize: RootSize?
+    }
+
+    private let ttl: TimeInterval
+    private let clock: @Sendable () -> Date
+    private let probe: Probe
+    private let environment: [String: String]
+    private var cache: [String: CacheEntry] = [:]
+    private var toolUnavailableReason: String?
+    private(set) var probeCount = 0
+
+    public init(
+        ttl: TimeInterval = SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor.defaultTTL,
+        clock: @escaping @Sendable () -> Date = { Date() },
+        probe: @escaping Probe = { SimulatorDisplayTopologyProbe.run(udid: $0) },
+        environment: [String: String] = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment
+    ) {
+        self.ttl = ttl
+        self.clock = clock
+        self.probe = probe
+        self.environment = environment
+    }
+
+    /// `rootSize` is the size of the AX root a caller just fetched. On a
+    /// multi-display device a root size that differs from the one the
+    /// cached answer was probed with bypasses that answer: the app moved to
+    /// another display (a fold from Device Hub or another process) or its
+    /// scene changed shape, inside the TTL (R157-02). The same root size
+    /// seen again does not re-probe, and a single-display answer stays
+    /// permanent.
+    public func state(for udid: String, fresh: Bool = false, rootSize: RootSize? = nil) -> SimulatorDisplayTopologyState {
+        if let raw = environment[Self.disableEnvironmentKey]?.lowercased(),
+           ["0", "false", "no", "off"].contains(raw)
+        {
+            return .unavailable(reason: "disabled by \(Self.disableEnvironmentKey)=\(raw)")
+        }
+        if let reason = toolUnavailableReason {
+            return .unavailable(reason: reason)
+        }
+
+        let now = clock()
+        if !fresh, let entry = cache[udid] {
+            if let topology = entry.state.topology, !topology.isMultiDisplay {
+                return entry.state
+            }
+            let rootChanged = rootSize != nil && rootSize != entry.rootSize
+            if now.timeIntervalSince(entry.checkedAt) < ttl, !rootChanged {
+                return entry.state
+            }
+        }
+
+        probeCount += 1
+        let state = probe(udid)
+        if case .unavailable(let reason) = state, reason.contains("subcommand") {
+            toolUnavailableReason = reason
+        }
+        cache[udid] = CacheEntry(state: state, checkedAt: now, rootSize: rootSize ?? Self.carriedRootSize(from: cache[udid], to: state))
+        return state
+    }
+
+    /// The root size a probe without one keeps from the previous entry: only
+    /// while the active display and its rotation are unchanged, since the
+    /// root size describes that display. A probe that sees another active
+    /// display drops it, so the next root size re-probes (R157-02).
+    private static func carriedRootSize(from previous: CacheEntry?, to state: SimulatorDisplayTopologyState) -> RootSize? {
+        guard let previous, let rootSize = previous.rootSize,
+              let old = previous.state.topology?.activeIntegrated,
+              let new = state.topology?.activeIntegrated,
+              old.uniqueID == new.uniqueID, old.rotation == new.rotation
+        else { return nil }
+        return rootSize
+    }
+
+    /// Drops the cached answer for `udid` so the next query re-probes.
+    public func invalidate(udid: String) {
+        cache[udid] = nil
+    }
+}

+/// iOS Simulator backend for `sim-use ios rotate`: turns the device so the
+/// display that hosts the app shows the requested interface orientation.
+/// Works on single-display simulators (Purple GSEvent) and on multi-display
+/// ones such as iPhone Duo (orientation picker report). Work record:
+/// docs/ai/010-display-routing/000-plan.md.
+public struct IOSSimRotateCommand: SimUseExecutableCommand {
+    public struct ExecutionResult: Codable, CommandAdvisoryProviding {
+        public let rotate: PostureController.RotateOutcome
+        public var commandAdvisory: CommandAdvisory? = nil
+
+        private enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
+            case rotate
+        }
+    }
+
+    public static let configuration = CommandConfiguration(
+        commandName: "rotate",
+        abstract: "Rotate the iOS Simulator to an interface orientation.",
+        discussion: """
+        Orientations are interface orientations — the same names the \
+        `describe-ui` header uses: portrait, landscape-left, \
+        landscape-right, portrait-upside-down. The command turns the \
+        device so the display that hosts the app shows that orientation, \
+        then reads the result back from CoreDevice.
+
+        An app that does not support the orientation stays as it is; the \
+        command then succeeds with an advisory that names the orientation \
+        the interface kept. Refused during a Resize Mode session, which is \
+        portrait-only.
+
+        A rotation changes the screen geometry, so the cached describe-ui \
+        snapshot is cleared; run `describe-ui` again before `tap @N`.
+
+        Examples:
+          sim-use ios rotate landscape-left --device UDID
+          sim-use ios rotate portrait --json --device UDID
+        """
+    )
+
+    @Argument(help: "portrait, landscape-left, landscape-right, or portrait-upside-down.")
+    public var orientation: String
+
+    @Option(name: .customLong("timeout"), help: "Seconds to wait for CoreDevice to confirm the rotation (default 5).")
+    public var timeout: Double = 5
+
+    @OptionGroup public var device: DeviceOptions
+
+    @OptionGroup public var json: JSONOutputOptions
+
+    public var jsonOutput: Bool { json.enabled }
+
+    public init() {}
+
+    public mutating func resolveDeferredArguments() throws {
+        if let arg = try DeviceOptions.selectExplicit(device: device.device, udid: device.udid),
+           PlatformRouter.looksLikeAndroid(arg) {
+            throw CLIError(errorDescription: HIDKeyCommandHelp.androidUnsupportedMessage(verb: "ios rotate", udid: arg))
+        }
+        try device.resolve()
+    }
+
+    public var simulatorUDIDForDaemon: String? { device.resolved }
+
+    public func validate() throws {
+        guard DisplayOrientation(rawValue: orientation) != nil else {
+            let names = DisplayOrientation.allCases.map(\.rawValue).joined(separator: ", ")
+            throw ValidationError("Orientation must be one of: \(names) (got '\(orientation)').")
+        }
+        guard timeout > 0, timeout <= 60 else {
+            throw ValidationError("--timeout must be between 0 and 60 seconds.")
+        }
+    }
+
+    public func format(_ result: ExecutionResult) -> CommandOutput {
+        let outcome = result.rotate
+        guard let reached = outcome.orientation else {
+            return .line("Sent device orientation \(outcome.deviceOrientation); the result could not be read back.")
+        }
+        let display = outcome.posture?.activeDisplay.map { " on display \($0.name)" } ?? ""
+        if outcome.confirmed {
+            return .line("Rotated to \(reached)\(display) (device \(outcome.deviceOrientation)).")
+        }
+        return .line("Not rotated: the interface\(display) stayed \(reached) (\(outcome.requested) not accepted).")
+    }
+
+    public func execute() async throws -> ExecutionResult {
+        let logger = SimUseLogger()
+        try await performGlobalSetup(logger: logger)
+        guard let target = DisplayOrientation(rawValue: orientation) else {
+            throw ValidationError("Unknown orientation '\(orientation)'.")
+        }
+        let (outcome, advisory) = try await PostureController.rotate(
+            udid: device.resolved, target: target, timeout: timeout, logger: logger
+        )
+        return ExecutionResult(rotate: outcome, commandAdvisory: advisory)
+    }
+}

+/// A display whose app scene is smaller than the display and placed at
+/// `offset` (UI points of the display's interface). The probe answers like
+/// the hit-test: panel points in, the element's scene frame out.
+private final class InsetScreen: @unchecked Sendable {
+    let native: NativePortraitSize
+    let orientation: DisplayOrientation
+    let offset: CGPoint
+    let elements: [CGRect]
+    /// Elements outside the scene, in display UI points (the status bar).
+    let displayElements: [CGRect]
+    private let lock = NSLock()
+    private var count = 0
+
+    init(native: NativePortraitSize, orientation: DisplayOrientation, offset: CGPoint, elements: [CGRect], displayElements: [CGRect] = []) {
+        self.native = native
+        self.orientation = orientation
+        self.offset = offset
+        self.elements = elements
+        self.displayElements = displayElements
+    }
+
+    var probes: Int { lock.lock(); defer { lock.unlock() }; return count }
+
+    func probe(_ panelPoint: CGPoint) -> [String: Any]? {
+        lock.lock(); count += 1; lock.unlock()
+        let display = orientation.framebufferToUI(panelPoint, native: native)
+        if let decoy = displayElements.first(where: { $0.contains(display) }) {
+            return ["role": "AXImage", "frame": ["x": decoy.minX, "y": decoy.minY, "width": decoy.width, "height": decoy.height] as [String: Any]]
+        }
+        let scene = CGPoint(x: display.x - offset.x, y: display.y - offset.y)
+        guard let hit = elements.first(where: { $0.contains(scene) }) else { return nil }
+        return ["role": "AXButton", "frame": ["x": hit.minX, "y": hit.minY, "width": hit.width, "height": hit.height] as [String: Any]]
+    }
+}

+// MARK: - Cached state after a posture change (R157-01)
+
+@Suite("PostureController — cached routing state after a posture change")
+struct PostureCacheRefreshTests {
+    /// Answers `first` on the first probe and `.inactive` after it: a
+    /// session that a fold ended.
+    final class EndingSession: @unchecked Sendable {
+        private let lock = NSLock()
+        private var calls = 0
+        let first: ResizableAppSessionState
+        init(first: ResizableAppSessionState) { self.first = first }
+        func probe() -> ResizableAppSessionState {
+            lock.lock(); defer { lock.unlock() }
+            calls += 1
+            return calls == 1 ? first : .inactive
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Test("a fold re-reads the Resize Mode session instead of reporting the cached one")
+    func foldRefreshesSession() async throws {
+        let ending = EndingSession(first: .active(session))
+        let sessions = ResizableAppSessionMonitor(probe: { _ in ending.probe() }, environment: [:])
+        let topologies = topologyMonitor(.available(try topology("duo-open")))
+        #expect(await sessions.state(for: "U").session == session) // warm cache
+        let now = await PostureController.postureChanged(udid: "U", topologyMonitor: topologies, sessionMonitor: sessions)
+        #expect(now == nil)
+        guard case .secondary = await RoutingDisplayResolver.current(udid: "U", sessionMonitor: sessions, topologyMonitor: topologies) else {
+            Issue.record("expected the inner display after the session ended")
+            return
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Test("rotate checks CoreDevice for a session, not a cached answer")
+    func rotateRechecksSession() async throws {
+        let ending = EndingSession(first: .active(session))
+        let sessions = ResizableAppSessionMonitor(probe: { _ in ending.probe() }, environment: [:])
+        #expect(await sessions.state(for: "U").session == session) // warm cache
+        try await PostureController.assertNoResizeSession(udid: "U", sessionMonitor: sessions)
+    }
+}

+// MARK: - AX root evidence refreshes the topology (R157-02)
