+@Suite("SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor — AX root size refreshes a multi-display answer")
+struct TopologyRootEvidenceTests {
+    final class Fixtures: @unchecked Sendable {
+        private let lock = NSLock()
+        private var current: SimulatorDisplayTopologyState
+        init(_ state: SimulatorDisplayTopologyState) { current = state }
+        func set(_ state: SimulatorDisplayTopologyState) { lock.lock(); current = state; lock.unlock() }
+        func get() -> SimulatorDisplayTopologyState { lock.lock(); defer { lock.unlock() }; return current }
+    }
+
+    private typealias RootSize = SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor.RootSize
+
+    @Test("an unfold seen in a new AX root re-probes inside the TTL and routes to the inner display")
+    func newRootReprobes() async throws {
+        let device = Fixtures(.available(try topology("duo-folded")))
+        let frozen = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 0)
+        let topologies = SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor(ttl: 60, clock: { frozen }, probe: { _ in device.get() }, environment: [:])
+        let sessions = sessionMonitor(.inactive)
+
+        // Folded: the cover's root warms the cache.
+        let folded = await RoutingDisplayResolver.current(
+            udid: "U", rootSize: RootSize(width: 466, height: 678), sessionMonitor: sessions, topologyMonitor: topologies
+        )
+        #expect(folded == .main)
+        #expect(await topologies.probeCount == 1)
+
+        // Unfolded out of band; the next fetch sees the inner root.
+        device.set(.available(try topology("duo-open")))
+        let open = await RoutingDisplayResolver.current(
+            udid: "U", rootSize: RootSize(width: 669, height: 951), sessionMonitor: sessions, topologyMonitor: topologies
+        )
+        guard case .secondary(let display) = open else {
+            Issue.record("expected the inner display, got \(open)")
+            return
+        }
+        #expect(display.name == "LCD-1")
+        #expect(open.interfaceOrientation == .landscapeLeft)
+        #expect(await topologies.probeCount == 2)
+
+        // Touch input now goes to the inner display's digitizer.
+        let route = try #require(try open.hidRoute())
+        #expect(route.digitizerTarget == 3)
+
+        // The same root again rides the cache.
+        _ = await RoutingDisplayResolver.current(
+            udid: "U", rootSize: RootSize(width: 669, height: 951), sessionMonitor: sessions, topologyMonitor: topologies
+        )
+        #expect(await topologies.probeCount == 2)
+
+        // Folding back changes the root again (inner → cover) and re-probes.
+        device.set(.available(try topology("duo-folded")))
+        let back = await RoutingDisplayResolver.current(
+            udid: "U", rootSize: RootSize(width: 466, height: 678), sessionMonitor: sessions, topologyMonitor: topologies
+        )
+        #expect(back == .main)
+        #expect(await topologies.probeCount == 3)
+    }
+
+    @Test("a rootless probe that sees another active display drops the old root association (R157-02 follow-up)")
+    func rootlessProbeDropsStaleRoot() async throws {
+        let device = Fixtures(.available(try topology("duo-open")))
+        let frozen = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 0)
+        let topologies = SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor(ttl: 60, clock: { frozen }, probe: { _ in device.get() }, environment: [:])
+        let sessions = sessionMonitor(.inactive)
+        let inner = RootSize(width: 669, height: 951)
+
+        // Inner display active; `ui` warms the cache with the inner root.
+        _ = await RoutingDisplayResolver.current(udid: "U", rootSize: inner, sessionMonitor: sessions, topologyMonitor: topologies)
+        #expect(await topologies.probeCount == 1)
+
+        // Folded out of band; a posture report probes without a root.
+        device.set(.available(try topology("duo-folded")))
+        _ = await topologies.state(for: "U", fresh: true)
+        #expect(await topologies.probeCount == 2)
+
+        // Unfolded again; the next `ui` brings the inner root back. The
+        // cached cover answer must not ride on the old inner root.
+        device.set(.available(try topology("duo-open")))
+        let routing = await RoutingDisplayResolver.current(udid: "U", rootSize: inner, sessionMonitor: sessions, topologyMonitor: topologies)
+        #expect(await topologies.probeCount == 3)
+        guard case .secondary(let display) = routing else {
+            Issue.record("expected the inner display, got \(routing)")
+            return
+        }
+        #expect(display.name == "LCD-1")
+        #expect(routing.interfaceOrientation == .landscapeLeft)
+        #expect(try routing.hidRoute()?.digitizerTarget == 3)
+    }
+
+    @Test("a rootless probe that sees the same active display keeps the root association")
+    func rootlessProbeKeepsValidRoot() async throws {
+        let frozen = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 0)
+        let state = SimulatorDisplayTopologyState.available(try topology("duo-open"))
+        let topologies = SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor(ttl: 60, clock: { frozen }, probe: { _ in state }, environment: [:])
+        let inner = RootSize(width: 669, height: 951)
+        _ = await topologies.state(for: "U", rootSize: inner)
+        _ = await topologies.state(for: "U", fresh: true)
+        _ = await topologies.state(for: "U", rootSize: inner)
+        #expect(await topologies.probeCount == 2)
+    }
+
+    @Test("a single-display answer stays permanent whatever the root size")
+    func singleDisplayIgnoresRoot() async throws {
+        let topologies = SimulatorDisplayTopologyMonitor(probe: { _ in .available(try! topology("iphone17")) }, environment: [:])
+        _ = await topologies.state(for: "U", rootSize: RootSize(width: 402, height: 874))
+        _ = await topologies.state(for: "U", rootSize: RootSize(width: 560, height: 874))
+        _ = await topologies.state(for: "U", rootSize: RootSize(width: 874, height: 402))
+        #expect(await topologies.probeCount == 1)
+    }
+}

+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+@testable import iOSSimBackend
+import Foundation
+import Testing
+
+// iPhone 12 mini: UI space 375x812, pixels / scale 360x780. The AX
+// hit-test consumes UI-METRIC points on native-portrait AXES (verified
+// live on iOS 26.4: querying the un-scaled UI point returns the element
+// at that point, while the pixels/scale-shrunk point lands ~4% off),
+// whereas HID dispatch normalizes against pixels/scale. These tests pin
+// the two transforms apart.
+private let mini = NativePortraitSize(width: 360, height: 780)
+private let miniScale = UIPointScale(native: mini, uiPortrait: (width: 375, height: 812))!
+
+private func miniCalibration(_ orientation: DisplayOrientation) -> OrientationCalibration {
+    OrientationCalibration(
+        orientation: orientation,
+        native: mini,
+        uiScale: miniScale,
+        probesUsed: 1,
+        advisory: nil
+    )
+}
+
+@Suite("Probe vs HID space on display-downscaled devices")
+struct DownscaledProbeSpaceTests {
+    @Test("portrait probes pass through un-scaled")
+    func portraitProbeIdentity() {
+        // The Settings toolbar Dictate button center: the probe must
+        // query exactly this UI point — shrinking it into the HID metric
+        // would hit the neighbouring row.
+        let p = miniCalibration(.portrait).probeCGPoint(CGPoint(x: 317.5, y: 760))
+        #expect(p == CGPoint(x: 317.5, y: 760))
+    }
+
+    @Test("portrait HID dispatch carries the metric scale")
+    func portraitHIDScales() {
+        let calibration = miniCalibration(.portrait)
+        #expect(!calibration.isIdentity)
+        let p = calibration.hidCGPoint(CGPoint(x: 187.5, y: 674.5))
+        #expect(abs(p.x - 180) < 0.001)
+        #expect(abs(p.y - 674.5 * 780 / 812) < 0.001)
+    }
+
+    @Test("landscape probes rotate on the UI-sized canvas, HID on the scaled one")
+    func landscapeProbeAndHIDDiverge() {
+        let ui = CGPoint(x: 100, y: 200)
+        // Axes only, on the 375x812 canvas: (375 − 200, 100).
+        let probe = miniCalibration(.landscapeRight).probeCGPoint(ui)
+        #expect(abs(probe.x - 175) < 0.001)
+        #expect(abs(probe.y - 100) < 0.001)
+        // HID additionally shrinks into the 360x780 metric.
+        let hid = miniCalibration(.landscapeRight).hidCGPoint(ui)
+        #expect(abs(hid.x - (360 - 200 * 360 / 375)) < 0.001)
+        #expect(abs(hid.y - 100 * 780 / 812) < 0.001)
+    }
+
+    @Test("wrappedProbe forwards portrait probe points untouched")
+    @MainActor
+    func wrappedProbePortrait() async throws {
+        final class Box: @unchecked Sendable { var received: CGPoint? }
+        let box = Box()
+        let probe = miniCalibration(.portrait).wrappedProbe { p in
+            box.received = p
+            return nil
+        }
+        _ = try await probe(CGPoint(x: 317.5, y: 760))
+        #expect(box.received == CGPoint(x: 317.5, y: 760))
+    }
+}

+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+import Foundation
+import Testing
+
+// Live coverage for multi-display simulators (docs/ai/010-display-routing):
+// `ios fold`, and every read path while the app is on the iPhone Duo inner
+// display. Needs a booted iPhone Duo (Xcode 27.1+). The suite reads the
+// display list from devicectl first and skips itself (not fails) on a
+// simulator with one integrated display, so it can sit in the default
+// suite list; `make e2e-ios-duo` picks a Duo and runs it there.
+//
+// The suite leaves the device unfolded or folded as it found it.
+
+@Suite("ios fold (multi-display simulators)", .serialized, .enabled(if: isE2EEnabled))
+struct FoldTests {
+    private static func json(_ text: String) throws -> [String: Any] {
+        let start = try #require(text.firstIndex(of: "{"), "expected JSON, got: \(text.prefix(300))")
+        return try #require(
+            try JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(text[start...].utf8)) as? [String: Any],
+            "expected JSON, got: \(text.prefix(300))"
+        )
+    }
+
+    /// Integrated displays and the active one, read from devicectl directly
+    /// so the gate does not depend on the code under test. Nil when
+    /// devicectl cannot answer.
+    private static func integratedDisplays(udid: String) async -> (count: Int, activeIsPrimary: Bool?)? {
+        guard let (output, _) = try? await CommandRunner.run(
+            "xcrun devicectl device info displays --device \(udid) --json-output - --timeout 5 --quiet 2>/dev/null",
+            allowFailure: true
+        ),
+            let json = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(output.utf8)) as? [String: Any],
+            let displays = (json["result"] as? [String: Any])?["displays"] as? [[String: Any]]
+        else { return nil }
+        let integrated = displays.filter { ($0["type"] as? [String: Any])?["integrated"] != nil }
+        let active = integrated.first { $0["active"] as? Bool == true }
+        return (integrated.count, active.map { $0["primary"] as? Bool == true })
+    }
+
+    /// The UDID when it is a multi-display simulator; nil (skip) otherwise.
+    private static func duoUDID() async throws -> String? {
+        let udid = try TestHelpers.requireSimulatorUDID()
+        guard let displays = await integratedDisplays(udid: udid), displays.count > 1 else { return nil }
+        return udid
+    }
+
+    private static func fold(_ posture: String, udid: String) async throws -> [String: Any] {
+        let simUse = try TestHelpers.getSimUsePath()
+        let (output, exitCode) = try await CommandRunner.run(
+            "\(simUse) ios fold \(posture) --json --udid \(udid) 2>/dev/null", allowFailure: true
+        )
+        #expect(exitCode == 0, "ios fold \(posture) failed: \(output)")
+        return try #require(try json(output)["data"] as? [String: Any])
+    }
+
+    /// Runs `body` and puts the hinge back where it was.
+    private static func preservingPosture(udid: String, _ body: () async throws -> Void) async throws {
+        let wasFolded = await integratedDisplays(udid: udid)?.activeIsPrimary ?? true
+        do {
+            try await body()
+        } catch {
+            _ = try? await TestHelpers.runSimUseCommandAllowFailure("ios fold \(wasFolded ? "closed" : "open")", simulatorUDID: udid)
+            throw error
+        }
+        _ = try? await TestHelpers.runSimUseCommandAllowFailure("ios fold \(wasFolded ? "closed" : "open")", simulatorUDID: udid)
+    }
+
+    @Test("closed and open are confirmed by the active display; no argument reports the posture")
+    func foldRoundTrip() async throws {
+        guard let udid = try await Self.duoUDID() else { return }
+        try await Self.preservingPosture(udid: udid) {
+            let closed = try await Self.fold("closed", udid: udid)
+            #expect(closed["confirmed"] as? Bool == true)
+            let closedActive = try #require((closed["posture"] as? [String: Any])?["activeDisplay"] as? [String: Any])
+            #expect(closedActive["primary"] as? Bool == true)
+            #expect(await Self.integratedDisplays(udid: udid)?.activeIsPrimary == true)
+
+            let open = try await Self.fold("open", udid: udid)
+            #expect(open["confirmed"] as? Bool == true)
+            let openActive = try #require((open["posture"] as? [String: Any])?["activeDisplay"] as? [String: Any])
+            #expect(openActive["primary"] as? Bool == false)
+            #expect(await Self.integratedDisplays(udid: udid)?.activeIsPrimary == false)
+
+            let report = try await Self.fold("", udid: udid)
+            #expect(report["requested"] == nil)
+            let posture = try #require(report["posture"] as? [String: Any])
+            #expect((posture["integratedDisplays"] as? [String])?.count == 2)
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Test("an intermediate angle reports the display it observed")
+    func halfOpen() async throws {
+        guard let udid = try await Self.duoUDID() else { return }
+        try await Self.preservingPosture(udid: udid) {
+            _ = try await Self.fold("closed", udid: udid)
+            let half = try await Self.fold("half", udid: udid)
+            #expect(half["confirmed"] as? Bool == true)
+            #expect(half["hingeAngle"] as? Double == 130)
+            // From closed, a jump to 130° opens the inner display (plan E21).
+            let active = try #require((half["posture"] as? [String: Any])?["activeDisplay"] as? [String: Any])
+            #expect(active["primary"] as? Bool == false)
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Test("unfolded: describe-ui names the inner display and its interface size; screenshot captures it")
+    func innerDisplayReadPaths() async throws {
+        guard let udid = try await Self.duoUDID() else { return }
+        let simUse = try TestHelpers.getSimUsePath()
+        try await TestHelpers.launchPlaygroundApp(to: "tap-test")
+        try await Self.preservingPosture(udid: udid) {
+            _ = try await Self.fold("open", udid: udid)
+            _ = try await TestHelpers.runSimUseCommand("ios rotate landscape-left", simulatorUDID: udid)
+
+            let (output, _) = try await CommandRunner.run("\(simUse) ui --json --no-raw --udid \(udid) 2>/dev/null")
+            let envelope = try Self.json(output)
+            let data = try #require(envelope["data"] as? [String: Any])
+            let display = try #require(data["display"] as? [String: Any])

+private func render(_ name: String) throws -> Outline {

+// Live coverage for `sim-use ios rotate` (docs/ai/010-display-routing).

+// (docs/ai/010-display-routing, S4). On an iPhone Duo with a Playground

+// and tab chrome in a vertical bar: the outline lists it as `[Trailing …]`
+// (portrait) or `[Leading …]` (landscape-right), and `@N` taps from that

+// same screen keeps its horizontal bars and no side region appears.

+@Suite("Outline side bars", .serialized, .enabled(if: isE2EEnabled))
+struct SideBarOutlineTests {
+    private static func outline(udid: String) async throws -> String {
+        try await CommandRunner.run("\(try TestHelpers.getSimUsePath()) ui --udid \(udid)").output
+    }
+
+    /// The `@N` alias on the line of `region` whose text contains `needle`.
+    private static func alias(of needle: String, in region: String, outline: String) -> String? {
+        var inRegion = false
+        for line in outline.components(separatedBy: "\n") {
+            if line.hasPrefix("[") { inRegion = line.hasPrefix("[\(region)") }
+            guard inRegion, line.contains(needle) else { continue }
+            return line.split(separator: " ").first { $0.hasPrefix("@") }.map(String.init)
+        }
+        return nil
+    }
+
+    private static func lastAction(udid: String) async throws -> String? {
+        let text = try await outline(udid: udid)
+        guard let line = text.components(separatedBy: "\n").first(where: { $0.contains("\"Last action: ") }),
+              let start = line.range(of: "\"Last action: ")
+        else { return nil }
+        return "Last action: " + line[start.upperBound...].prefix { $0 != "\"" }
+    }
+
+    private static func isMultiDisplay(udid: String) async -> Bool {
+        let result = try? await TestHelpers.runSimUseCommandAllowFailure("ios fold closed", simulatorUDID: udid)
+        return result?.exitCode == 0
+    }
+
+    @Test("the bar is its own region and its aliases land", arguments: [
+        ("portrait", "Trailing"),
+        ("landscape-right", "Leading"),
+    ])
+    func barRegion(orientation: String, region: String) async throws {
+        let udid = try TestHelpers.requireSimulatorUDID()
+        let multiDisplay = await Self.isMultiDisplay(udid: udid)
+        try await TestHelpers.launchPlaygroundApp(to: "chrome-test")
+        _ = try await TestHelpers.runSimUseCommandAllowFailure("ios rotate \(orientation)", simulatorUDID: udid)
+        // Let the rotation animation finish before the outline is read; a
+        // mid-animation snapshot once sent both alias taps astray.
+        try await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 1_500_000_000)
+        do {
+            let text = try await Self.outline(udid: udid)
+            // `make e2e-ios-duo` with an iOS 27.1+ SDK Playground sets this.
+            let expectBar = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["SIM_USE_E2E_EXPECT_SIDE_BAR"] == "1"
+            #expect(!expectBar || !multiDisplay || text.contains("[\(region)"), "expected a \(region) region: \(text)")
+            guard multiDisplay, text.contains("[\(region)") else {
+                // A single display, or an SDK that keeps horizontal bars.
+                #expect(!text.contains("[Leading") && !text.contains("[Trailing"), "unexpected side region: \(text)")
+                _ = try? await TestHelpers.runSimUseCommandAllowFailure("ios rotate portrait", simulatorUDID: udid)
+                return
+            }
+            #expect(Self.alias(of: "#BackButton", in: region, outline: text) != nil, "BackButton in the bar: \(text)")
+
+            let search = try #require(Self.alias(of: "\"Search\"", in: region, outline: text), "Search tab in the bar: \(text)")
+            try await TestHelpers.runSimUseCommand("tap \(search)", simulatorUDID: udid)
+            try await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 600_000_000)

+            try await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 600_000_000)

+            throw error
+        }
+        _ = try? await TestHelpers.runSimUseCommandAllowFailure("ios rotate portrait", simulatorUDID: udid)
+    }

+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+@testable import iOSSimBackend
+import Foundation
+import SimUseCore
+import Testing
+
+// A calibration taken from the describe-ui snapshot is used for UI-space
+// coordinates only when hit-tests under it still find the snapshot's
+// elements where the snapshot put them (docs/ai/010-display-routing, S3).
+// The snapshot path reads no tree, so it has no other way to notice a
+// display that changed (a Resize Mode session that started), a rotation
+// or another screen.
+
+private let native = NativePortraitSize(width: 402, height: 874)
+private let screenArea = 402.0 * 874.0
+
+// Small, off-center elements in portrait UI space.
+private let elements: [CGRect] = [
+    CGRect(x: 16, y: 120, width: 56, height: 56),
+    CGRect(x: 330, y: 120, width: 56, height: 56),
+    CGRect(x: 16, y: 780, width: 56, height: 56),
+    CGRect(x: 330, y: 780, width: 56, height: 56),
+]
+
+private func calibration(_ orientation: DisplayOrientation) -> OrientationCalibration {
+    OrientationCalibration(orientation: orientation, native: native, probesUsed: 0, advisory: nil)
+}
+
+/// A screen whose UI is in `truth` and shows `shown`: a hit-test at a
+/// framebuffer point returns the shown element there, else the window.
+private func screen(_ truth: DisplayOrientation, shown: [CGRect]) -> OrientationCalibrator.HitTestProbe {
+    { point in
+        let ui = truth.framebufferToUI(point, native: native)
+        let rect = shown.first { $0.contains(ui) } ?? CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 402, height: 874)
+        return ["frame": ["x": rect.minX, "y": rect.minY, "width": rect.width, "height": rect.height]]
+    }
+}
+
+@Suite("Snapshot calibration confirmation")
+struct SnapshotConfirmationTests {
+    @Test("the snapshot's elements are still in place")
+    func confirmed() async {
+        let ok = await OrientationCalibrator.confirms(
+            calibration(.portrait), discriminators: elements, sceneArea: screenArea,
+            probe: screen(.portrait, shown: elements))
+        #expect(ok)
+    }
+
+    @Test("another display answers with a full-screen element (a session that started)")
+    func otherDisplay() async {
+        let ok = await OrientationCalibrator.confirms(
+            calibration(.portrait), discriminators: elements, sceneArea: screenArea,
+            probe: screen(.portrait, shown: []))
+        #expect(!ok)
+    }
+
+    @Test("the device rotated since the snapshot")
+    func rotated() async {
+        // The four corners are point-symmetric, so the rotated screen
+        // shows an element at every probed corner — just not the one the
+        // snapshot put there.
+        let ok = await OrientationCalibrator.confirms(
+            calibration(.portrait), discriminators: elements, sceneArea: screenArea,
+            probe: screen(.portraitUpsideDown, shown: elements))
+        #expect(!ok)
+    }
+
+    @Test("no probe-able element confirms nothing")
+    func noDiscriminators() async {
+        let ok = await OrientationCalibrator.confirms(
+            calibration(.portrait), discriminators: [CGRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 402, height: 874)],
+            sceneArea: screenArea, probe: screen(.portrait, shown: elements))
+        #expect(!ok)
+    }
+
+    @Test("a probe error counts as a miss")
+    func probeError() async {
+        let ok = await OrientationCalibrator.confirms(
+            calibration(.portrait), discriminators: elements, sceneArea: screenArea,
+            probe: { _ in throw CLIError(errorDescription: "gone") })
+        #expect(!ok)
+    }
+
+    @Test("one probe-able element needs one hit")
+    func singleDiscriminator() async {
+        let ok = await OrientationCalibrator.confirms(
+            calibration(.portrait), discriminators: [elements[0]], sceneArea: screenArea,
+            probe: screen(.portrait, shown: elements))
+        #expect(ok)
+    }
+
+    @Test("the snapshot fits only the scene it was taken of", arguments: [
+        (CGSize(width: 402, height: 874), CGSize(width: 402, height: 874), true),
+        // A rotation swaps the sides; the probes decide the orientation.
+        (CGSize(width: 874, height: 402), CGSize(width: 402, height: 874), true),
+        // The iPhone Duo inner display: interface 951x669, panel-sized root.
+        (CGSize(width: 951, height: 669), CGSize(width: 669, height: 951), true),
+        // A Resize Mode session resized from 560x1200 to 560x667 (R161-01).
+        (CGSize(width: 560, height: 1200), CGSize(width: 560, height: 667), false),
+        (CGSize(width: 386, height: 678), CGSize(width: 466, height: 678), false),
+    ])
+    func sceneSize(snapshot: CGSize, root: CGSize, expected: Bool) {
+        #expect(OrientationCalibrator.snapshotFits(screen: snapshot, rootSize: root) == expected)
+    }
+
+    @Test("an unknown root size does not fit")
+    func unknownRoot() {
+        #expect(!OrientationCalibrator.snapshotFits(screen: CGSize(width: 402, height: 874), rootSize: nil))
+    }
+}

+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+import Foundation
+import SimUseCore
+import Testing
+
+// Live coverage for explicit coordinates in UI space by default
+// (docs/ai/010-display-routing, S3): numbers read from `ui` land where
+// they were read, in every orientation, for tap, swipe, touch and the
+// two-finger verbs; `--coordinate-space native` keeps the old mapping.
+// Runs on any booted iOS simulator — on an iPhone Duo, fold it closed
+// first or run it on the inner display; both route through the same
+// calibration. Every test restores portrait on the way out.
+
+@Suite("Explicit coordinates default to UI space", .serialized, .enabled(if: isE2EEnabled))
+struct UICoordinateDefaultTests {
+    private static let corners = [
+        "corner-top-leading", "corner-top-trailing", "corner-bottom-leading", "corner-bottom-trailing",
+    ]
+
+    private static func restorePortrait(udid: String) async {
+        _ = try? await TestHelpers.runSimUseCommandAllowFailure("ios rotate portrait", simulatorUDID: udid)
+    }
+
+    /// Rotates and reports whether the device really turned: an iPhone
+    /// may keep portrait for `portrait-upside-down`.
+    private static func rotate(_ orientation: String, udid: String) async throws -> Bool {
+        let simUse = try TestHelpers.getSimUsePath()
+        let (output, _) = try await CommandRunner.run(
+            "\(simUse) ios rotate \(orientation) --json --udid \(udid) 2>/dev/null", allowFailure: true
+        )
+        try await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 800_000_000)
+        return output.contains("\"confirmed\":true") || output.contains("\"confirmed\" : true")
+    }
+
+    private static func element(_ id: String, in root: UIElement) -> UIElement? {
+        UIStateParser.findElement(in: root, withIdentifier: id)
+    }
+
+    private static func center(of id: String, in root: UIElement) throws -> (x: Int, y: Int) {
+        let frame = try #require(element(id, in: root)?.frame, "no frame for \(id)")
+        return (Int((frame.x + frame.width / 2).rounded()), Int((frame.y + frame.height / 2).rounded()))
+    }
+
+    /// The app's own frame: the gesture areas are `Color.clear` views
+    /// that the accessibility tree does not expose.
+    private static func screen(_ root: UIElement) throws -> UIElement.Frame {
+        try #require(root.frame, "no root frame")
+    }
+
+    private static func value(_ id: String, udid: String) async throws -> String? {
+        element(id, in: try await TestHelpers.getUIState(simulatorUDID: udid))?.value
+    }
+
+    /// These screens set a screen-level accessibility identifier, which
+    /// replaces every child's id: find their read-outs by label.
+    private static func label(containing prefix: String, udid: String) async throws -> String? {
+        UIStateParser.findElementContainingLabel(
+            in: try await TestHelpers.getUIState(simulatorUDID: udid), containing: prefix
+        )?.label
+    }
+
+    /// Runs `body` in `orientation` and restores portrait afterwards,
+    /// also on failure, so later suites start upright. Skips when the
+    /// device keeps another orientation.
+    private static func inOrientation(
+        _ orientation: String, screen: String, udid: String,
+        _ body: () async throws -> Void
+    ) async throws {
+        try await TestHelpers.launchPlaygroundApp(to: screen)
+        do {
+            if try await rotate(orientation, udid: udid) {
+                try await body()
+            }
+        } catch {
+            await restorePortrait(udid: udid)
+            throw error
+        }
+        await restorePortrait(udid: udid)
+    }
+
+    @Test("tap -x/-y read from ui lands on every corner", arguments: [
+        "portrait", "landscape-left", "landscape-right", "portrait-upside-down",
+    ])
+    func cornerTaps(orientation: String) async throws {
+        let udid = try TestHelpers.requireSimulatorUDID()
+        try await Self.inOrientation(orientation, screen: "orientation-test", udid: udid) {
+
+            let root = try await TestHelpers.getUIState(simulatorUDID: udid)
+            for corner in Self.corners {
+                let point = try Self.center(of: corner, in: root)
+                try await TestHelpers.runSimUseCommand("tap -x \(point.x) -y \(point.y)", simulatorUDID: udid)
+                try await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 400_000_000)
+                #expect(try await Self.value("corner-last-tapped", udid: udid) == corner, "\(orientation): tap at \(point) should hit \(corner)")
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Test("without a describe-ui snapshot the tree calibrates instead")
+    func cornerTapWithoutSnapshot() async throws {
+        let udid = try TestHelpers.requireSimulatorUDID()
+        try await Self.inOrientation("landscape-right", screen: "orientation-test", udid: udid) {
+
+            let root = try await TestHelpers.getUIState(simulatorUDID: udid)
+            let point = try Self.center(of: "corner-bottom-trailing", in: root)
+            OutlineCache.invalidate(udid: udid)
+            try await TestHelpers.runSimUseCommand("tap -x \(point.x) -y \(point.y)", simulatorUDID: udid)
+            try await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: 400_000_000)
+            #expect(try await Self.value("corner-last-tapped", udid: udid) == "corner-bottom-trailing")
+        }
+    }
+
+    @Test("--coordinate-space native keeps the native mapping")
+    func nativeOptOut() async throws {
+        let udid = try TestHelpers.requireSimulatorUDID()
+        try await Self.inOrientation("landscape-left", screen: "orientation-test", udid: udid) {
+

+# 009.001 — Touch and accessibility routing to the Resizable display
+
+## Context
+
+This record ended with a stop-gap: detect the session and refuse touch
+input, because the scene's place inside the 7680x4320 canvas was unknown and
+a spike that swept digitizer targets 0–10 did not land a tap. The iPhone Duo
+work (docs/ai/010-display-routing) revisited the spike on 2026-10-16.
+
+## Change
+
+- **The scene sits at the canvas origin.** Send `IndigoDigitizerEvent` with
+  `target = <Resizable display id>` (4 on iPhone 17, 5 on iPhone Duo) and
+  normalize the scene point against the canvas **in pixels**:
+  `ratio = point × pointScale / 7680x4320`, i.e. `point / 2560x1440`.
+  Verified on iPhone 17 / iOS 27.0 and the folded Duo, scenes 560x874 and
+  375x667: Playground `Tap Location: (450, 650)` for a tap at (450, 650).
+- **Why the spike missed:** `FBSimulatorIndigoHID.screenRatio` computes
+  `point × scale / screenSize`, so it expects pixels; the spike passed the
+  2560x1440 point canvas, which made every ratio three times too large.
+  Likely, not reproduced.
+- **Accessibility:** the AX translator takes `displayId = <Resizable display
+  id>`; its point hit-test is in scene points. No offset or canvas is needed.
+- **Detection still comes from `devicectl device info appResize`.** The
+  `Resizable` display stays `active: false` with the backlight off during a
+  session, so the display list cannot tell.
+- Shipped in the 010 S2 change: touch verbs and hit-tests are routed instead
+  of refused; `ui` drops its `resizable_app_session` advisory and names the
+  display in the header; `record-video` / `stream-video` still refuse.
+  A `ui` whose root is the device's own size re-checks a cached session, so
+  touches return to the main display when the session ends.
+- The Tier 3 plan above (bump idb, upstream `DisplaySelection`, the guest
+  bridge) is not needed for Resize Mode: a small patch to the pinned idb
+  (`patches/idb/display-routing.patch`) adds the digitizer target and the AX
+  display id.
+
+Refs: docs/ai/010-display-routing/000-plan.md (E14–E18, E33).

+# 010 — Display routing (iPhone Duo, Resize Mode) and device rotation: Plan
+
+| | |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Status** | In progress (S1 #157; S2 in review) |
+| **Anchor date** | 2026-10-16 |
+| **Primary PRs** | — |
+| **Related** | [009-resizable-app-session](../009-resizable-app-session/000-investigation.md) (#143; this plan replaces its tier-1 guard with real routing), [002-ios-orientation-self-calibration](../002-ios-orientation-self-calibration/000-design.md), [001 dtuhidd short-lived clients](../001-daemon-and-hid-lifecycle/001-dtuhidd-short-lived-clients.md), facebook/idb#965, facebook/idb#980 |
+
+## Background
+
+sim-use binds every iOS primitive to the **main display**: HID digitizer
+target 0, the `displayClass 0` framebuffer, and AX translator `displayId: 0`
+(see 009). Two Xcode 27 features put the app on another display:
+
+1. **iPhone Duo** (Xcode 27.1): a foldable device with two integrated displays. Only one is active at a time.
+2. **Resize Mode** (`devicectl device appResize`, Xcode 27, any iPhone): the frontmost app moves to the virtual `Resizable` display (#143).
+
+`devicectl device info displays` on the two test devices:
+
+| Device | Display | `displayId` | Type | Pixels (@3x) | Notes |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| iPhone Duo / 27.1 | `LCD` (cover) | 1 | integrated | 1398x2034 | `primary`; active when folded |
+| | `LCD-1` (inner) | 3 | integrated | 2007x2853 | active when unfolded; `rot90` when the device is portrait |
+| | `Resizable` | 5 | virtual | 7680x4320 | Resize Mode |
+| iPhone 17 / 27.0 | `LCD` | 1 | integrated | 1206x2622 | `primary` |
+| | `Resizable` | 4 | virtual | 7680x4320 | Resize Mode |
+
+The `Resizable` display is always listed, also with no session, and it stays
+`active: false` with the backlight off **during** a session. Only
+`devicectl device info appResize` tells that a session is active (009).
+
+Measured on `main` @ `81c3089` (idb `1f6943f8`) with the Duo unfolded:
+
+| Surface | Result |
+| --- | --- |
+| `screenshot` | Black image of the cover framebuffer (1398x2034) |
+| `tap`, `swipe` | Print success, deliver nothing |
+| `ui` tree fetch | Correct frames in UI space (951x669) |
+| `ui` header and regions | Screen reported as 669x951, so the region bands are wrong |
+| Point hit-test (`ui --point`, orientation calibration, collapsed-children recovery) | Fails: "No translation object returned"; the advisory fires every time; the sidebar is lost behind `Group (0,0 951x669)` |

+Under Resize Mode, 009 records the same failures and ships a guard that
+refuses touch verbs.

+The Duo cover display also changes the layout model. iOS 27 puts the status

+| E12 | iPhone 16 Pro / iOS 18.6, Xcode 27.1 and 26.6 devicectl | Works | — |
+| E13 | iPhone Duo / iOS 27.1 | Prints success, no effect (inner stays `rot90`) | Works (E2) |
+
+- The iOS 27.1 runtime accepts only the iPhone Duo device type (`simctl create` with iPhone 17 fails: "Incompatible device"), so E10–E13 cannot separate "runtime" from "device type".
+- Names differ: `devicectl` uses **device** orientation, sim-use outline tags use **interface** orientation. Device `landscapeRight` gave `rot90`, and `sim-use ui` printed `(landscape-left)` for it.
+- A portrait-only app (SpringBoard on iPhone) stays `rot0` after the device rotates.
+
+## Goals
+
+- **One routing model** for every display that hosts the app: `tap`, `swipe`, `touch`, `gesture`, `ui` (including `--point`) and `screenshot` work on the Duo inner display **and** in a Resize Mode session on any iPhone. This closes #143.
+- `sim-use ios fold` controls the hinge of a foldable simulator and confirms the result.
+- `sim-use ios rotate` rotates **any** iOS simulator and reports the resulting interface orientation.
+- The outline groups side-rail chrome (back button, status bar) correctly on the Duo displays.
+- Detection is by **capability and state**, not by model name, so a future device works without new code.
+- A single-display device with no Resize Mode session keeps byte-identical behavior and output, except for the deliberate coordinate-default change in S3.
+- `record-video` and `stream-video` capture the routing display.
+- Explicit iOS coordinates default to UI space, the space of the outline and of Android.
+
+**Non-goals**
+
+- An in-simulator helper process (upstream `SimulatorFrameworkBridge`, `axbridge`).
+- Physical Duo devices (`ios-device` backend).
+- Android `fold` / `rotate`. A follow-up issue is filed after this stack; the verb arguments stay portable.
+
+## Design
+
+### Display topology
+
+New `SimulatorDisplayTopology` in `Sources/iOSSimBackend/Sim/`. It decodes the
+devicectl displays document into `[SimulatorDisplay]` (`displayId`,
+`uniqueId`, `name`, `type`, `primary`, `active`, `rotation`, `bounds`,
+`pointScale`). `SimulatorDisplayGeometry` copies the upstream shape
+(`rot0…rot270`, `unrotatedPointSize`, `pointSize`, `unrotatedPoint(from:)`) so
+the idb migration only replaces the data source.
+
+### Routing display resolution
+
+One function decides where the app is, from two inputs that already have
+cheap probes: the topology (E9) and the Resize Mode session state
+(`ResizableAppSessionMonitor`, `Sources/iOSSimBackend/Sim/ResizableAppSession.swift`).
+
+| State | Routing display | Digitizer target | Normalization canvas | Point transform | AX `displayId` |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Resize Mode session active | `Resizable` (virtual) | its `displayId` | canvas points (`bounds / pointScale`) | none: scene point at canvas origin (E14) | its `displayId` (E15) |
+| More than one integrated display | the `active` integrated display | its `displayId` | panel points | rotation (E4) | its `displayId` (E6, E7) |
+| Otherwise | main display | 0 (unchanged) | unchanged | existing calibrator | 0 (unchanged) |
+
+- The last row is the current code path. It runs when there is one integrated display and no session, so traditional devices are not affected.
+- Both monitors cache in the daemon with a short TTL, and refresh after `fold`, `rotate`, and when the AX root size disagrees with the cached geometry. They share one devicectl client.
+- On a non-main routing display, the orientation comes from devicectl `currentOrientation` (a session is always `rot0`, E17), so `OrientationCalibrator` probes are skipped.
+- A sanity check fails loudly when a hit-test at the routing display centre returns nothing or a pid other than the frontmost app.
+
+### Transport changes
+
+- **HID:** an idb patch (`patches/idb/`, applied by `apply_idb_patches` in `scripts/build.sh`) adds a per-event digitizer `target` and an explicit normalization canvas **in pixels** (E18) to `FBSimulatorDTUHIDTransport`.
+- **AX:** the same patch replaces the fixed `displayId: 0` in `FBAXTranslationRequest.swift` with a parameter.
+- **Screenshot:** `simctl io … --display=<uniqueId>` (E8, E16) for any non-main routing display. 009 already does this for sessions.
+
+### Fold verb
+
+`sim-use ios fold <closed|half|open|DEGREES> [--device] [--json]`, iOS-only,
+registered in `Sources/iOSSimBackend/Verbs/IOSSimCommand.swift`. The
+vendor-event XPC lives in sim-use (`iOSSimBackend/HID/`), not in the idb patch.
+After the send, the verb polls the topology. The signal is the display
+`active` flag, not `backlightState` (E19, E20).
+
+- `closed` (0°) expects the primary display and `open` (180°) a non-primary integrated display. Both are deterministic (E21). The verb fails on timeout.
+- `half` (130°) and `DEGREES` have no fixed expectation (E21). The verb waits until the topology is stable, then reports the active display it observed. It does not claim the angle, because sim-use cannot measure it (E22).
+- A fold wakes a locked device to the lock screen (E20). The verb reports this; it does not unlock.
+- It refuses devices with one integrated display.
+
+### Rotate verb
+
+`sim-use ios rotate <portrait|landscape-left|landscape-right|portrait-upside-down> [--device] [--json]`.
+
+- **Names are interface orientations**, the same names as the outline tag (`DisplayOrientation` in `Sources/iOSSimBackend/A11y/DisplayOrientation.swift`). The verb maps them to the device orientation it sends.
+- **Transport by capability:** one integrated display → `devicectl device orientation set` (E10–E12); more → the orientation vendor event (E2, E13).
+- **Result:** the verb reads back the device orientation and the routing display `currentOrientation`. It fails when the device orientation did not change. When the app does not support the orientation, it succeeds with an advisory and reports the real interface orientation.
+- During a Resize Mode session the verb refuses: sessions are portrait-only (E17).
+
+### Outline layout
+
+`OutlineFormatter` (`Sources/iOSSimBackend/Normalizer/OutlineFormatter.swift`)
+takes the screen size from the AX root frame and assigns `Top` / `Content` /
+`Bottom` by `yBandInset = 120`. Two changes:
+
+1. **Screen size:** on a non-main routing display, use the routing geometry `pointSize` (the scene size for a session), not the AX root frame (669x951 vs the real 951x669).
+2. **Side rail:** add `Trailing` and `Leading` regions. They are **evidence-gated** (`Sources/iOSSimBackend/Normalizer/OutlineSideBars.swift`): an anchor (`BackButton` identifier, or a tab role `RadioButton`/`Tab`) in a 120 pt edge strip, at least two elements of its column stacked vertically, and the app's wide content clear of the bar's inner edge. The S4 evidence (E40) showed that the first idea — an anchor outside the top band — fails: in cover landscape-left the back button is in the top band. The bar's entries are listed after the bands. Without the evidence the output does not change.
+
+The iOS host AX gives no stable navigation-bar role. On the cover display the
+navigation bar is `AXGroup` with a localized role description (`导航栏`), so
+`declaredRegionKinds` cannot detect it.
+

+| Decision | Options considered | Chosen because |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Do it now on the pinned idb (A), migrate idb later (B) | Wait for B; do A now | B is a full API migration (no FB* name survives since `1f6943f8`; facebook/idb#980 double rotation). A's CLI surface, tests and E2E carry over; the throwaway part is the patch, the devicectl source and the XPC transport. Upstream B does not cover Resize Mode (009), so A's session routing must survive B in some form |
+| One routing model for the Duo and Resize Mode | Duo only, #143 later | E14–E16: the same target / `displayId` / per-display screenshot mechanism works for the virtual display; only the canvas rule differs |
+| No process inside the simulator | upstream guest for the AX id; host-side devicectl id | E7 shows the ids are the same; product rule: nothing added to the simulator. For B: an upstream PR for a host-only identity source, or a small patch |
+| Fold confirmation by the `active` flag; no angle claim | Measure the angle like upstream (`monitormotion`); trust the send | E21: 0° and 180° are deterministic. Reading `monitormotion` needs a CoreDevice client that the pinned idb does not have; the migration can add it |
+| Fold transport in sim-use, not in the idb patch | idb patch; sim-use | Keeps the patch to the parameters that B makes native |
+| Gate on state ("session active", "more than one integrated display") | Model name (`iPhone Duo`); device-type table; display count including virtual | Future devices work with no change; the `Resizable` display is listed on every Xcode 27 iPhone, so a raw display count would include every device |
+| Side-rail regions gated by evidence | Device table ("Duo = trailing rail"); AX roles; geometry only | Roles are localized; tables need a change for each device; evidence keeps single-display output identical |
+| Authoritative rotation from devicectl on a non-main routing display | Keep hit-test calibration | E9 is cheap and exact; probes do not reach the display without routing anyway |
+| Rotation transport chosen by capability: Purple GSEvent on one integrated display, orientation picker report on more | devicectl `orientation set`; always vendor event; try one, then the other | E10–E13, E23: Purple needs no devicectl, runs on every runtime tested and is what upstream idb uses when the runtime has no device motion; devicectl is still used to read the result back. A fallback chain doubles the latency of the failure case |
+| Rotation planning by a transport offset learned from the read-back | Per-display offset; hard-coded Duo table | E24: rotations and the reported device orientation share one frame, only the picker value is offset. The first guess (0 primary, 1 secondary) is corrected once when the device turned to the wrong side; a report that did not change teaches nothing (E25) and ends as "not accepted" with an advisory, never a second guess |
+| Fold and rotate clear the describe-ui snapshot | Keep it, rely on the stale-snapshot advisory | A fold moves the app to another display with another geometry; a cached `@N` would tap the old coordinates on the new display |

+| S2: a device-sized AX root re-checks a cached active session | Keep the 5 s staleness | Touches are now routed, not refused: a stale "active" would send them to the display the app left (E33) |
+| Rotate takes interface orientation names | Device orientation names (devicectl) | Agents read the outline tag, which is interface orientation; one vocabulary in the CLI |
+| `fold` and `rotate` are iOS-only verbs (`sim-use ios …`) | Top-level verbs now | No Android implementation yet. Android emulators can fold and rotate, so the arguments stay portable for a later top-level verb (owner decision, 2026-10-16: Android later, separate issue) |

Same space as the outline and Android; devicectl orientation removes the calibration-failure risk that kept `native` the default. Breaking for callers that hand-write native coordinates on a rotated or downscaled device: `CHANGELOG` `Changed` |
+| Record and stream the routing display in this stack | Refuse until the idb migration | Owner decision 2026-10-16: complete Duo support |

+| S3: UI-space calibration from the `ui` snapshot first, used only when probes confirm the snapshot's elements are in place | Tree every time (+~75 ms, E34); snapshot like `tap @N` (no confirmation) | The snapshot path reads no tree, so the routing display comes from the daemon cache: after a Resize Mode session ended, an unconfirmed snapshot calibration sent the first tap to the gone `Resizable` display (`ResizeModeTests.firstExplicitTapFollowsSession` red without the confirmation). Two in-place hits within four probes cost a few ms (E35); any doubt falls back to the tree, which re-checks the routing (R158-03). CoreDevice is not consulted on this path |
+| S3: the snapshot path reads the frontmost app's root frame (`FBAccessibilityElement.frame()`, no tree) and requires the snapshot to fit it (R161-01) | Element confirmation only; tree every time | A resized Resize Mode session (560x1200 → 560x667) kept its top controls, so element probes confirmed the old 1200 pt canvas and a gesture started below the scene. +| S3: split `touch --down` / `--up` take UI coordinates, each half calibrated | Keep `ui` atomic-only (split form would need `native`) | With `ui` as the default, the old rule would reject every split touch. Each half maps the point through the orientation at its own time, which is where the user sees it |
+| S3: `gesture` pinch/rotate centre and canvas in UI space, every sample mapped | Keep native portrait for multi-touch presets | The calibration is affine, so mapping each interpolated sample keeps lines and arcs; the directional presets already use the UI canvas (#66) |

+| Device Hub closed: make it work if possible, else refuse with the requirement | Must work | Owner decision 2026-10-16 |

+#!/bin/bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+# Runs the iOS E2E suites that cover multi-display simulators on an iPhone
+# Duo (docs/ai/010-display-routing). The default suite list also contains
+# them, but they skip on a single-display simulator; this wrapper picks a
+# Duo so they run.
+#
+#   SIMULATOR_UDID               use this simulator instead of picking one
+#   SIM_USE_TEST_DEVELOPER_DIR   Xcode used for simctl and the Playground build.
+#                                Default: the newest installed Xcode 27.1 or later,
+#                                whose SDK adapts the app fully to the Duo. An
+#                                Xcode 27.0 build keeps out of the cover display's
+#                                status bar strip, and an older SDK runs centred.
+#
+# Arguments are suite filters passed to scripts/test-runner.sh; without
+# them the display-routing suites and the suites whose expectations do not
+# depend on an iPhone layout run. DescribeUITests and SwipeTests pin iPhone 17
+# frames, TypeTests a US keyboard layout, and TapTests taps the back button by
+# its title, which an iOS 27.1 SDK app on the Duo cover display does not show:
+# the button moves into the vertical bar with an empty label.
+
+set -euo pipefail
+cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
+
+if [[ -z "${SIMULATOR_UDID:-}" ]]; then
+    # Prefer a booted iPhone Duo, then any available one.
+    SIMULATOR_UDID=$(xcrun simctl list devices available -j | python3 -c '
+import json, sys
+devices = [d for runtime in json.load(sys.stdin)["devices"].values() for d in runtime if "iPhone Duo" in d["name"]]
+devices.sort(key=lambda d: d["state"] != "Booted")
+print(devices[0]["udid"] if devices else "")
+')
+fi
+if [[ -z "$SIMULATOR_UDID" ]]; then
+    echo "No iPhone Duo simulator found. Install the iOS 27.1 runtime (Xcode 27.1+) and create one, or set SIMULATOR_UDID." >&2
+    exit 1
+fi
+export SIMULATOR_UDID
+
+if [[ -z "${SIM_USE_TEST_DEVELOPER_DIR:-}" ]]; then
+    best=""
+    best_version=""
+    for app in /Applications/Xcode*.app; do
+        version=$(defaults read "$app/Contents/Info" CFBundleShortVersionString 2>/dev/null || true)
+        [[ -z "$version" ]] && continue
+        # Keep the highest version that is 27.1 or later.
+        if [[ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "27.1" "$version" | sort -V | head -1)" == "27.1" ]] &&
+           [[ -z "$best_version" || "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$best_version" "$version" | sort -V | tail -1)" == "$version" ]]; then
+            best="$app/Contents/Developer"
+            best_version="$version"
+        fi
+    done
+    if [[ -n "$best" ]]; then
+        export SIM_USE_TEST_DEVELOPER_DIR="$best"
+        echo "Using Xcode $best_version for simctl and the Playground build ($best)"
+    fi
+fi
+
+# A Playground built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later shows the vertical bar
+# on the cover display, so SideBarOutlineTests must find it there.
+playground_xcode_version=$(defaults read "${SIM_USE_TEST_DEVELOPER_DIR:-$(xcode-select -p)}/../Info" CFBundleShortVersionString 2>/dev/null || true)
+if [[ -n "$playground_xcode_version" && "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "27.1" "$playground_xcode_version" | sort -V | head -1)" == "27.1" ]]; then
+    export SIM_USE_E2E_EXPECT_SIDE_BAR=1
+fi
+
+if [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then
+    set -- FoldTests RotateTests ResizeModeTests ScreenshotTests UICoordinateDefaultTests SideBarOutlineTests
+fi
+exec ./scripts/test-runner.sh "$@"

-**Symptom:** `tap`, `long-press`, `swipe`, `touch`, `gesture`, `multi-touch`, `paste --via-menu`, a `batch` with a touch step, `record-video` or `stream-video` fails with `A resizable app session (Xcode 27 Resize Mode) is active on simulator …` (`--json`: `ok: false` with a `hint`). `ui` prints `[i] A resizable app session … is active` (`--json`: `advisory.kind: resizable_app_session`) and its `App:` header shows a size that is not a real device size (`560x874`, `375x667`, `874x402` on an upright iPhone 17). `screenshot` prints `[i] Captured the 'Resizable' display …`.
+**Symptom:** The `ui` header ends in `display Resizable 560x874` (`--json`: a `data.display` object with `kind: virtual` and `resizableSession`), its size is not a real device size, and `screenshot` prints `[i] Captured the 'Resizable' display …`. `record-video` and `stream-video` fail with `… captures only the main display …`.
 
-**Why:** Xcode 27 can move the frontmost app of an iOS 27+ simulator onto a virtual display named `Resizable` and give it any size (Device Hub's resize button, or `xcrun devicectl device appResize start`). The main display then shows only the wallpaper, with SpringBoard frontmost. Simulator touch input, the main framebuffer and the accessibility point hit-test are all bound to the main display, so a tap would be reported as delivered and reach nothing — which is why sim-use refuses it. Keyboard input is device-wide and does reach the app. Issue: https://github.com/lycorp-jp/sim-use/issues/143.
+**Why:** Xcode 27 can move the frontmost app of an iOS 27+ simulator onto a virtual display named `Resizable` and give it any size (Device Hub's resize button, or `xcrun devicectl device appResize start`). sim-use detects the session and routes touch input, hit-tests and screenshots to that display. Video capture still reads only the main display, which shows the wallpaper. Issue: https://github.com/lycorp-jp/sim-use/issues/143.
 
 **Recipes:**
-1. Observe freely: `ui` is the app's own tree at the resized size (hit-test recovery and orientation calibration are skipped, so collapsed groups stay collapsed), and `screenshot` is redirected to the `Resizable` display. `record-video` and `stream-video` are refused — they can only capture the main display; record the app with `xcrun simctl io <udid> recordVideo --display=<uuid> <file.mov>` (the error's hint fills in the uuid). The `App:` header is the only place the scene's *actual* size shows — `appResize set` reports the size it asked for, which the scene may snap away from.
-2. Drive with the keyboard: `type`, Cmd+V `paste`, `key`, `key-combo`, `key-sequence` and keyboard-only `batch` runs work during a session. `paste --via-menu` is a long-press plus menu taps and is refused like a tap. Focus the field *before* starting the session, since focusing needs a tap.
-3. To tap, end the session: stop the `devicectl device appResize start` process (or rotate the device — rotation ends a session), re-run `ui`, then tap. The app returns to the device's native size.
-4. Never use `--point`/`-x -y` as a workaround — raw coordinates are refused like selectors, and `ui --point` describes SpringBoard, not the app.
-5. The check costs one `devicectl` query per device per 5 s. A session that just *started* is noticed by the next `ui`, selector tap, or touch step of a `batch` (a newly resized root frame bypasses the cache; a `batch` re-checks before every touch step) unless the scene is exactly the device's own size; a session that just *ended*, and standalone raw `-x/-y` taps right after a start, can see the previous answer for up to 5 s. `SIM_USE_RESIZE_SESSION_CHECK=0` disables the check (you are then back to silent no-op taps); the per-device daemon reads it at spawn time, so set it on the first command or pair it with `SIM_USE_NO_DAEMON=1`. This recipe needs sim-use 0.15.0 or newer — the preflight enforces it.
+1. Work as usual: `ui`, selectors, `@N`, `tap`, `swipe`, `gesture`, `type` and `screenshot` all act on the resized app. The `App:` header is the only place the scene's *actual* size shows — `appResize set` reports the size it asked for, which the scene may snap away from.
+2. Explicit `-x/-y` are scene points (the scene is never rotated).
+3. To record video, end the session (stop the `devicectl device appResize start` process), or record the display yourself with `xcrun simctl io <udid> recordVideo --display=<uuid> <file.mov>` (the error's hint fills in the uuid).
+4. The check costs one `devicectl` query per device per 5 s. A `ui` or selector tap whose root changed size re-reads it at once, so a session that just started or ended is noticed by the next `ui`. A raw `-x/-y` tap with no `ui` in between can see the previous answer for up to 5 s. `SIM_USE_RESIZE_SESSION_CHECK=0` disables the check; the per-device daemon reads it at spawn time.
+
+## iOS: iPhone Duo (multi-display simulator)
+
+**Symptom:** The `ui` header ends in `display LCD-1` (for example `App: Settings  951x669  (landscape-left, display LCD-1)`; `--json`: a `data.display` object). `record-video` and `stream-video` fail with `… captures only the main display …`.
+
+**Why:** The iPhone Duo simulator (Xcode 27.1) has two integrated displays. Folded, the app is on the cover display, the main one. Unfolded, it is on the inner display (`LCD-1`). sim-use routes touch input, hit-tests and screenshots to the display that hosts the app and takes its orientation from CoreDevice. Video capture still reads only the main display.
+
+**Recipes:**
+1. Check the posture: `sim-use ios fold --device <UDID>` names the active display and its orientation.
+2. Fold and unfold with `sim-use ios fold closed|open --device <UDID>`; rotate with `sim-use ios rotate <orientation>` (interface names, as the `ui` header prints them). Both clear the `ui` snapshot — re-run `ui` before `tap @N`.
+3. An iOS 27.1 SDK app puts its back button, trailing toolbar items, tab bar and status bar in a **vertical bar** on the cover display (and on the inner display in landscape). The outline lists it last, as `[Trailing  x>=N]` — `[Leading  x<=N]` when the cover is in landscape-right; its `@N` aliases tap as usual. The back button there has **no label**: tap it with `#BackButton`, not by the previous screen's title.
+4. Explicit `-x/-y` take the numbers `ui` prints on either display; `--coordinate-space native` means the inner panel's unrotated points.
+5. To record video, fold the device so the app is on the cover display.

release.body:
- The camera control works on every iPhone that has one, not only the iPhone Duo, and Device,
  Camera Control presses it. The item appears only for devices with the button. The simulator has
  no camera, so the device takes a screenshot.
- Choosing cover, half open or fully open on the iPhone Duo folds it smoothly to that angle instead
  of jumping, unless Reduce Motion is on. The device stays inside the window in every pose,
  standing ones included.
- The iPhone Duo's window moves to the screen the device is using sooner after a fold.
- Recording the iPhone Duo records the screen it is using, follows it through a fold, and keeps the
  picture the right way up.
- A window opens the way its device is already turned, instead of assuming it is upright.
- Restarting a device no longer leaves its window half connected. The iPhone Duo's fold buttons,
  cover screen and touches come back with the fold it was showing, and the clipboard sync picks up
  again.
- Device, Shut Down shuts a simulator down from the menu.
- Every menu action acts on the simulator in front, not on every open one, and ticks such as Stay
  On Top, Slow Animations and Connect Hardware Keyboard show that simulator's own setting.
- Favorite locations: save named coordinates in Settings and choose them from Features, Location.
- Screenshots and recordings each have their own folder in Settings, starting from the folder you
  had already chosen, and Save Screen can put the picture on the clipboard instead of in a file.
- Clipboard sync can be turned on or off in Settings as well as from the Edit menu, and the two stay
  in step.
- The screen shown while a device is shut down or starting stays inside its rounded corners.
- The Settings window can be resized, and scrolls.
- The disk image opens as an installer window: drag the app onto Applications. The mounted disk
  shows the app's icon.

Shut Down, favorite locations and the capture and clipboard settings were contributed by
@stephen-zeng.

## Requirements

macOS 14 or later, Apple silicon, and Xcode 26 or 27 with at least one iOS simulator runtime.

Apple silicon only, and not by preference: the simulator frameworks this app loads from Xcode ship
as `arm64e` with no Intel slice, so an Intel build would launch and then fail at the first framework
load.

## Known gaps

These are the ones worth knowing before you install it:

- **The windows are invisible to accessibility**: VoiceOver, window managers and scripting tools see
  the app and its menus but not its windows.
- **A device taller than your display** keeps its bottom edge off screen, where the pointer cannot
  reach it. Use Fit.
- **The compact layout below 340 points wide** is written and unit tested but has never been used by
  hand.
- **Other Apple platforms**: tvOS, watchOS and visionOS simulators are not supported.

## Verifying the download

The app is signed with a Developer ID certificate, notarized by Apple and stapled, so it launches
without a Gatekeeper warning. `SHA256SUMS` is attached; to check the DMG against it:

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
```

## Credits

Built after studying two MIT licensed projects, and better for both:
[Siniulator](https://github.com/kmagiera/Siniulator) by Krzysztof Magiera, and
[idb / FBSimulatorControl](https://github.com/facebook/idb) by Meta. What was adapted from each, down
to the individual constants, is listed in
[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](https://github.com/Mastersam07/OpenDeviceHub/blob/dev/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

## Tell me what breaks

If something does not work, please [open an issue](https://github.com/Mastersam07/OpenDeviceHub/issues/new/choose):
`odhub doctor` prints almost everything the bug form asks for.

> **Distribution notice:** The attached DMG is the official Rockxy binary distribution under the Rockxy Binary EULA. It runs in Community mode without a purchase and can unlock Pro. The public tag identifies the separate AGPL Community source edition for this product version; it is not represented as the complete build source for the DMG.

# Rockxy 0.41.0 (build 62)

## Added

- Explore the active traffic tab with Traffic Insights: spot slow requests and failures, compare traffic over time, find top apps and hosts, and export a Markdown report.
- Keep investigations organized in local Projects with saved traffic history, tab layouts, and filters. Project configuration can be imported and exported without moving captured traffic.
- Redact credentials and other sensitive values when exporting Rockxy sessions, HAR, CSV, or Postman files, while keeping the original captured session intact.
- Inspect recognized model API and Web3 RPC traffic with dedicated details, and find model API, Web3, gRPC, GraphQL, WebSocket, and HTTP exchanges through protocol labels and filters.
- Review nearby iPhone transfers in their own workspace while keeping the Mac's current traffic available.
- Apply HTTPS decryption and tunnel rules to specific apps, route traffic through an upstream proxy, import cURL into Compose, and copy requests as Swift, Python, JavaScript, or Go snippets.

## Changed

- Developer Setup is now a compact, target-aware workflow with clearer manual and automatic paths, certificate trust status, and more useful readiness and launch results.
- Server-Sent Events, NDJSON, and WebSocket exchanges appear while they are active, with stream and frame details updated as traffic arrives.
- Counts, sizes, durations, dates, and translated interface text follow the app language and the Mac's region more consistently.
- Large captures remain more responsive through reduced per-row analysis and paced Traffic Insights updates.

## Fixed

- Imports keep every request instead of trimming to the live history limit. HAR exports preserve content types, timestamps, readable streamed bodies, and measured durations more reliably.
- Repeat, Edit and Repeat, and Compose results appear as inspectable traffic rows; replay also handles plain HTTP and edited destinations correctly.
- WebSocket upgrades, plain HTTP inside CONNECT tunnels, upstream proxy routing, and TLS failure reporting are more reliable and easier to diagnose.
- Header rules work alongside Map Local, Block, and other rules; invalid headers no longer break a response, and No Caching prevents clients from reusing stale responses.
- Redacted shares, MCP exports, and inspections of compressed responses better protect credentials while keeping useful debugging details visible.
- Developer Setup no longer hits the reported window layout crash, and proxy stop/recovery handles delayed helper responses without requiring a second click.
- Perpetual license access remains available after its included update period instead of falling back to Community.

release.body:
An AI-friendly iOS/iPadOS automation service. Tell your agent *"My iPhone is running iCTRL at :8200 — figure out how to drive it."* and it reads the on-device manual and takes it from there. Works with any agent that can make HTTP requests: OpenClaw, Hermes, Minis, Claude Code, Codex and others. ## Downloads ### Which IPA do I need? | File | Needed? | What it is | |---|---|---| | `iCTRLUITests-Runner.ipa` | **Required** | The automation engine. It serves the JSON-RPC API that agents and clients call, and must be running. | | `iCTRL.ipa` | Optional | A companion app for tasks on the phone itself:
• mount the Developer Disk Image without a Mac, and remount it after a reboot
• start and stop the runner
• choose who can reach the runner (this device only / LAN / LAN + nearby)
• see and revoke authorized clients
• read the runner's log live | Skip `iCTRL.ipa` if you mount the Developer Disk Image with Xcode or StikDebug, and manage the runner from its notification or a computer. With a free Apple ID you get three sideloaded apps, and SideStore uses one of them. Install StikDebug *or* the iCTRL app alongside the runner, not both. Both IPAs are unsigned for distribution (ad-hoc, no provisioning profile). Sign them when you install: - **Free Apple ID:** the latest SideStore signs and installs them. Older SideStore releases skip the nested `.xctest`, and the runner then crashes on launch. - **Paid account:** `Scripts/sign-ipa.sh -i iCTRLUITests-Runner.ipa` The runner also needs the Developer Disk Image mounted (Xcode, StikDebug or the iCTRL app). The [README](https://github.com/OpenMinis/iCTRL#installation) covers the whole setup. ## What's new since 1.97.1 ### Nearby discovery: no address to type - **Reach the phone without an address.** Turn on **📡 Nearby Discovery** from the runner's notification or the iCTRL app (it needs Remote Access). Clients can then find the phone: - on the LAN, from any OS; - from a Mac over Apple peer-to-peer Wi-Fi (AWDL), with no shared network at all. The phone only needs Wi-Fi switched on, not joined to anything. - **New client commands:** `python3 ictrl_rpc.py scan` lists discovered phones, and `--nearby ""` replaces `--host`. The first call pairs with the phone (approve once on the phone). - **Strict exposure:** - Nothing is announced on the network unless nearby discovery is on. - The AWDL listener accepts peer-to-peer connections only, and the main listener refuses them. - Nearby discovery can be switched **on** only from the phone itself (notification, iCTRL app or USB). - **Self-healing:** - Advertising follows Wi-Fi off and on, and recovers if the interface is recreated. - A failed listener is rebuilt. - The notification says why nearby discovery isn't ready yet (*turn on Wi-Fi*, *allow Local Network*). ### Who can reach the phone, at a glance - **The status notification's first line** shows one of: 🔒 This device only, 🌐 LAN reachable, or 📡 Nearby discoverable. - **The iCTRL app has a Visibility menu:** 🟢 This device only · safe / 🟡 LAN / 🟡 LAN + nearby. - **LAN addresses are real interfaces only.** VPN or proxy tunnel addresses such as `198.18.0.1` are no longer shown as the phone's address. ### Pairing and keys - **Every pairing is approved on the phone.** The "trusted for 10 minutes" shortcut is gone. - **Limits on requests:** - An unanswered request is refused after 60 s. - Only one request waits at a time, with a 15 s cooldown after a refusal. - Requests from the phone itself have their own slot, so a remote caller can't lock them out. - **Check the key.** The prompt shows a key fingerprint that the client also prints; allow only if they match. - **One key per device.** Clients store keys per device, so a phone paired once works over USB, the LAN and nearby without pairing again. Keys stored under an address by older clients are picked up automatically. - **Local Network permission.** The runner asks for it at launch and reports it. The iCTRL app warns when it's missing; without it, nearby discovery can't work even though LAN clients may still connect. ### iCTRL app - **Authorized Clients:** every key holder, where each last connected from (this device / USB, LAN, nearby, VPN), revoke one or all others. - **Runner Logs:** the runner's log, live, with pause, refresh and filter. - **Visibility menu** (above), and a warning when the runner lacks Local Network access. - **Share a pairing file to iCTRL** from Files, Mail, AirDrop or a chat app when the picker can't reach it. iCTRL confirms when it's stored, or says why it was refused. ### Clients - **Python client:** - Standard library only. LAN pairing no longer needs `pip install cryptography`. - Never sends iCTRL requests through an `http_proxy`. - If macOS Local Network privacy refuses the process, it relays nearby connections through the system `nc`. - **C CLI:** gets the same nearby support when built on macOS. The Linux static binary is rebuilt. ### Server and API - `GET /whoami` and an `X-ICTRL-Device` header on every response identify the device. - `config` adds `nearby_discovery` and `device_name`, and reports nearby status and LAN addresses. Each client's last address and source appear in its session entry. - `config` now validates every parameter before changing any. - A change that restarts the listener replies first instead of returning an empty response. - Read-only polling (`logs`, plain `config`) no longer fills the log. ### Known limitations - Nearby discovery over AWDL needs macOS on the client side. A phone whose screen is off may stop being discoverable over AWDL, as with AirDrop. - With nearby discovery on, iOS also announces the phone's own host name on the LAN, which often contains its owner's name. - Endpoints that need no key (`/schema`, `/skill`, `/remote`, `/whoami`, `/pair`) also answer over AWDL, and the screen stream is not encrypted on any channel. Full details: [#3](https://github.com/OpenMinis/iCTRL/pull/3). ## SHA-256 ``` d28fcb4775885a7161e8c7aa9f247aeb42fe1af1c7fcfc5ce1bbdb1b07b442f2 iCTRLUITests-Runner.ipa 7d9ceaad8eeb486e67d81a688e661f2278113d4ba4f7d3d73cff2f9973881ac7 iCTRL.ipa ```

## Release v2.7.1

### Changed

- Renamed the project from XcodeBuildMCP to MobileBuildMCP. The npm package, CLI binaries (`mobilebuildmcp`, `mobilebuildmcp-doctor`), Homebrew formula, `MOBILEBUILDMCP_*` environment variables, `mobilebuildmcp://` resource URIs, `mobilebuildmcp.output.*` structured output schema IDs, the `.mobilebuildmcp/config.yaml` project config directory, and the `~/Library/Developer/MobileBuildMCP` state directory all use the new name. The `xcodebuildmcp.com` domain is retired: structured output schema `$id` URLs now use `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getsentry/MobileBuildMCP/main/schemas/structured-output/`, documentation links point at the docs sources in the `getsentry/xcodebuildmcp.com` repository, and the MCP registry name is `io.github.getsentry/mobilebuildmcp`.
- Dictionary-shaped MCP inputs now use client-compatible wire representations ([#491](https://github.com/getsentry/XcodeBuildMCP/issues/491)). The `env` and `testRunnerEnv` inputs on build, launch, test, and session-default tools are arrays of `{ "key": "...", "value": "..." }` entries, while `xcode_ide_call_tool.arguments` is a JSON object string. MobileBuildMCP converts these values to their existing internal objects only after MCP input validation.

### Option A — Homebrew (no Node.js required)

Install:
```bash
brew tap getsentry/xcodebuildmcp
brew install mobilebuildmcp
```

MCP config:
```json
"MobileBuildMCP": {
  "command": "mobilebuildmcp",
  "args": ["mcp"]
}
```

### Option B — npm / npx (Node.js 18+)

Install:
```bash
npm install -g mobilebuildmcp@latest
```

MCP config:
```json
"MobileBuildMCP": {
  "command": "npx",
  "args": ["-y", "mobilebuildmcp@latest", "mcp"]
}
```

📦 **NPM Package**: https://www.npmjs.com/package/mobilebuildmcp/v/2.7.1

# Harness 0.8.4 — set_value, and type() stops lying about no-ops

A focused point release for one severe finding (WB-27 / W36): `act{type}` could not fill an `<input type="datetime-local">` behind a controlled React `onChange` — the field cleared and the create was silently dropped, while REST and Playwright both worked. Two failure modes hid behind it: reading `selectionStart` on a date/number/datetime-local input *throws* (aborting the whole insert), and a controlled component reverts any value not set the framework's way. Tool-surface change is additive.

## Highlights

### New `set_value(id, value)` web act

Addresses a Set-of-Mark id (the same parked registry `scroll_into_view` uses), focuses the element, drives the value through the native prototype setter — the React-value-tracker-correct path — dispatches `input` + `change`, blurs to commit, then **reads the value back** and reports whether it stuck. `<select>` matches by option value or visible label.

It's a distinct tool rather than a `value` argument on `type` because the contracts differ — keystroke-and-caret versus whole-value-and-verified — and a distinct tool advertises and refuses web-only cleanly. Wired end to end: the act vocabulary, `act_ui` schema, decoder, supervisor dispatch, settle profile, logging, replay, and previews. macOS/iOS refuse it explicitly for now — an AX value-set needs per-role verification, and a value-set that silently no-ops while reporting success is exactly the dishonesty this release is about.

### `type()` stops reporting no-ops as success

The typing JS now guards the `selectionStart` read and reports `{ had, changed }`: a no-op (no field focused, or a controlled/readonly field ignoring the insert) sets an honest driver detail pointing at `set_value`, instead of a clean "typed" over an unchanged screen. The mechanism is unchanged; it just stops lying. Best-effort by construction — a component that reverts on a *later* render still reads as changed here, which is why `set_value` exists. The JS returns only booleans, so the shared `fill_credential` path leaks no value.

### Verification

- **Suite 520 → 530 green.** New `WebValueEntryTests` runs the shipped JS against live-WKWebView fixtures: a controlled input that reverts a naive assignment but commits `set_value`'s, a datetime-local, a select by value and by label, the non-settable and stale paths, and the type no-op flag.
- **Live smoke** gains a set-value leg: the datetime persists through the controlled `onChange`, the select lands by label, and typing into a keystroke-ignoring field warns. Both smokes pass.

## JEV 多模态决策，进入手机点击加速的新阶段

AI Phone v0.8.0 将 JEV 接入 V3 缓存回放：把已有动作目标转换为当前画面中的编号候选，由多模态 Decisions 模型选择目标，再映射到设备坐标执行。Android、iOS、HarmonyOS 共用这条定位流程，并按平台使用各自的设备适配。

### 本次更新

- **JEV 普通点击定位**：截图与 UI 树生成候选编号，模型选择编号，程序计算并执行点击；输入、滚动、拖动等动作继续使用原 V3 定位，失败进入现有救援。
- **三端快速设备通道**：Android 使用 UiAutomator2 原生 JPEG、坐标点击与实时尺寸读取；HarmonyOS 使用原生截图及 UITest；iOS 使用 WDA 按需截图与点击适配。启动检查失败时保留原通道兜底。
- **统一开关**：`AI_PHONE_JEV_ENABLED` 控制 JEV 及其配套快速通道、稳定检测，默认关闭。另提供渠道、密钥及可选模型配置，请参阅 ENV 示例与轨迹缓存使用文档。
- **加载等待与截图复用**：JEV 可在明确加载迹象下请求有界等待；稳定图直接用于定位。等待刷新后定位仍失败时，救援承接最新定位图，避免根据旧画面决策。
- **定位证据**：日志展示实际编号标注模型输入图、所选编号、坐标和分段耗时；JEV 分支不重复上传画框前原图。
- **混合动作分流修复**：在加载原始缓存 Action 时确定定位路线，避免输入框检查生成的临时点击请求被 JEV 接管。
- **V3 回放节奏**：取消逐动作 after 留证截图，动作后观察调整为 200ms，最终断言前等待 2 秒。这部分为当前 V3 公共行为，不仅在 JEV 开启时生效。
- **文档与展示**：README 新增 JEV 原理图、真机连续执行动图和本地性能分段说明，前后端版本统一为 0.8.0。

### 性能与适用范围

已有 Android 实验中，候选标注与编码约 15–50ms，非模型点击链路中位耗时约 620ms；特定样本包含模型往返的一次点击达到约 0.99 秒。完整流程耗时仍由模型往返、页面加载、缓存动作与救援共同决定，这些样本不是每次请求的速度保证。

JEV 当前承接 V3 回放中的普通 Click，不替代任务规划或最终业务断言。模型选错、目标未出现等情况仍可能发生，现有救援及原链路继续保留。

### 配置

```dotenv
AI_PHONE_JEV_ENABLED=true
AI_PHONE_JEV_PROVIDER=openrouter
AI_PHONE_JEV_API_KEY=<your-provider-key>
AI_PHONE_JEV_MODEL=
```

`PROVIDER` 支持 `openrouter` / `openai`，模型留空使用对应渠道默认值。Android Agent 在 backend 目录安装可选依赖：`pip install -e '.[jev]'`。请求地址按渠道选择，超时为内部设置，无需填写额外 ENV。

### 验证

已完成 JEV、混合动作分流、三端关闭分支、截图与稳定通道、救援截图交接等回归测试，并通过 Web 构建。包含三端设备实验记录；最新关闭分支的 iOS 真机验证因设备锁屏未完成，不计为通过。

无新增数据库迁移。更新后需重启 Server 与 Agent，使新版配置和执行代码生效。

## Revyl CLI v0.1.178

### Installation

**Shell (macOS / Linux):**
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RevylAI/revyl-cli/main/scripts/install.sh | sh
```

**Homebrew (macOS):**
```bash
brew install RevylAI/tap/revyl
```

**pipx (cross-platform):**
```bash
pipx install revyl
```

**uv (cross-platform):**
```bash
uv tool install revyl
```

**pip:**
```bash
pip install revyl
```

The PyPI package contains the native CLI for the selected platform
and does not download a binary on first run.

**Direct download:**
Download the appropriate binary for your platform from the assets below.

**Revyl Computer (standalone):**
On macOS or Linux:
```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/RevylAI/revyl-cli/releases/latest/download/install-computer.sh | sh
```
The installer selects your platform, verifies the release checksum,
and installs to `~/.revyl/bin` without sudo. Restart your shell, or
run the PATH command it prints, then run `revyl-computer --help`.
On Windows, download `revyl-computer-windows-<arch>.exe` from the
assets below, verify its checksum, and rename it to
`revyl-computer.exe` in a directory on your PATH.
This separate CLI is not included in the package-manager installs above.

### Agent Skill

The agent skill is embedded in the binary. Install it with:
```bash
revyl skill install --cursor   # For Cursor
revyl skill install --claude   # For Claude Code
revyl skill install --codex    # For Codex
```

Or download `SKILL.md` from the assets below and place it manually.

### Checksums
See `checksums.txt` for SHA256 checksums of all binaries.

release.body:
[功能] 新增“快速模式”，可将原先 10 秒的刷新耗时降低到 3 秒以内，相关说明：https://qxh1ndiez2w.feishu.cn/wiki/BPihwfigUigWLQk1Epmc5SFenEe
[功能] 图层右键菜单中增加“刷新”按钮，可单独刷新某一个或某几个图层，从而避免缓慢的全局刷新（需将 LookinServer 配合更新至 1.2.7 或更高版本）
[鸣谢] 本次新功能由 @starFelix  提出想法，并通过 Github PR 贡献了核心代码。

-------

[Feature] Introducing "Fast Mode" to reduce the refresh time from the previous 10 seconds to within 3 seconds. Details: https://qxh1ndiez2w.feishu.cn/wiki/BPihwfigUigWLQk1Epmc5SFenEe
[Feature] Added a "Refresh" button in the right-click menu of layers, allowing users to individually refresh one or multiple layers to avoid slow global refresh (requires updating LookinServer to version 1.2.7 or higher).
[Acknowledgment] These new features were designed by @starFelix  and contributed the core code through the Github PR.
